articles.title: Michael van Gerwen stars in Grand Slam epic clash against Tom Sykes with TWO nine-darters to book semi-final spot
articles.summary: Michael van Gerwen and Tom Sykes both hit nine-darters in their quarter final at the Grand Slam; he will next face Gian van Veen, who came through a tough contest against Nathan Aspinall; watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Van Gerwen's nine-darter came in the opening leg and marked his first on Sky Sports since 2012. After two 180s, he pinned T20, T19, then D12 to end a 14-year wait for perfection and send the Wolverhampton crowd into a frenzy.

Despite the barrage from the Dutchman Sykes stayed composed, and in the sixth leg he replicated the three-time Grand Slam champion and hit nine perfect darts of his own. It even earned a wry smile from his opponent.

At that point, Van Gerwen was averaging 124 and Sykes 112, their levels so incredible they were hard to believe.

It is the third televised match to feature two nine-darters, adding to the 2010 Premier League tie between Phil Taylor and James Wade and the 2014 World Grand Prix contest between James Wade and Robert Thornton.

Eventually, Van Gerwen found a mid-match burst that was too much for Sykes to deal with and - with a bullseye finish - he sealed a 16-11 victory.

The 'Green Machine' is aiming to win his fourth Grand Slam title, adding to his 2015, 2016, and 2017 triumphs.

Sykes also comes out of the match with enormous credit as he averaged 101.50, provided 12 180s, and made his mark on an incredible debut.

In the semi-finals, Van Gerwen will take on his Dutch compatriot Gian van Veen after he held off a Nathan Aspinall comeback for a 16-14 victory.

"For everyone who's doubted me, I'm still here, don't worry," Van Gerwen told Sky Sports .

"No, no, I'm never going to run away. But of course I had tough times.

"It's been hard, it's been tough. I've not been producing what I'm capable of, but today I think I played a fantastic game, and then to play against Tom Sykes, because he was amazing, you know what I mean?

"I need to give him the credit as well."

Following the nine-darters that highlighted a sensational opening six legs, Sykes and Van Gerwen continued to battle and provide brilliance.

Sykes reeled in a Big Fish in the ninth leg and looked to be taking the contest to Van Gerwen. However, Van Gerwen then put his foot on the gas.

His purple patch saw him go from 8-6 behind to 12-9 ahead, winning five out of the next six legs.

That run increased to eight out of nine legs, a break of throw helping Van Gerwen into a 14-9 advantage before the 'Castleford Tiger' could stop the rot.

After holding his throw to go one leg from the semi-finals, Van Gerwen then broke Sykes' throw with a massive bullseye checkout to ensure he returns for what is set to be an epic day on Sunday.

Van Veen scraped through to victory over Aspinall in what was an incredibly hard-fought contest.

In the opening session, Van Veen was allowed to take a 4-1 lead without any pressure thanks to Aspinall's poor scoring on the trebles.

The second session followed a similar pattern to the first with Aspinall unable to muster his best level. That saw Van Veen find a run of three legs in a row, a big 116 checkout on tops from 'The Asp' stopping the Dutchman from moving five legs ahead.

However, Aspinall then came to life. From 7-3 down, he found three breaks of throw and won four out of the next five legs to make the game a real contest at 8-7. He continued to hang onto Van Veen, with both players experiencing a drop in scoring, to bring the match to 11-9.

Nothing was coming easy to Van Veen and he suffered over 30 trebleless visits. That saw Aspinall in control and finally level the game at 12-12.

From there, both players held their throw well until the crucial 30th leg. Aspinall fell away on his own throw and so with the finish line firmly in his sights, Van Veen nailed a maximum and then wrapped things up on D8 to make it into his first Grand Slam semi-final.

Watch the Grand Slam of Darts (November 14-22) and World Darts Championship (December 11-January 3) all live on Sky Sports. Stream darts and more through NOW with no contract.

articles.title: Army pranks Navy ahead of annual rivalry football game with 'Go Army' message in Midshipmen's home stadium
articles.summary: The two service academies have a long history of 'spirit missions' in their rivalry, which has often involved kidnapping mascots.
articles.body:
Army and Navy don't meet in their annual football matchup for another three weeks. But the Black Knights fired a strong opening salvo at their rival service academy with a memorable prank on Saturday.

Prior to Navy's home game versus Memphis at Navy-Marine Corps Stadium in Annapolis, Maryland, Army supporters moved and spray-painted seats in the upper deck that read "GO NAVY" to read "GO ARMY."

Considering those seats are bolted down, rearranging the blue and yellow seats took some time and planning.

The prank was discovered hours before Navy was set to kick off against Memphis at 12 p.m. ET. That provided enough time for staffers — 20 of them, according to ESPN's Morgan Uber — to restore the upper-deck seats to their original message supporting the Midshipmen.

Security cameras viewed the cadets — who were in uniform — moving the seats in the stadium at 1 a.m. ET, The Athletic's Chris Vannini reports . The prank took approximately three hours to complete.

Staffers were dispatched to the stadium around 6 a.m. and took nearly four hours to put the seats back in their original arrangement. But everything was back in its rightful place by the time gates opened to allow fans in at 10 a.m.

Saturday's seat stunt is the latest in a long history of pranks — or "spirit missions," as the two academies call them — between the rival military branches ahead of their annual football clash.

That includes Navy cadets stealing four of Army's mule mascots in 1991. But Navy has had its goat mascot stolen by Army students several times, the most recent attempt in 2021. (However, the wrong goat was stolen in that raid.) A formal agreement was drafted in 1992 to prohibit mascot stealing .

Three years ago, the Midshipmen dropped ping-pong balls with "Beat Army" and "Fly Navy" from three small planes onto the West Point campus.

Air Force has also been the target of pranks from Army and Navy. In 2018, cadets stole a falcon from the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs. Yet that prank turned out badly as the falcon injured itself beating its wings against the dog crate it was stored in.

Perhaps inspired by having their home stadium invaded by rival pranksters, the Midshipmen scored an upset 38-34 victory over Memphis . Ranked No. 24 in the AP Top 25 , the Tigers came into Saturday's context with an 8-2 record and wins in three of their past four games to lead the American conference. That run included a 49-22 home victory over Army in Week 9.

By contrast, Navy took a 3-6 (2-4 in conference) mark into the matchup. Quarterback Jackson Gutierrez rushed for 241 yards and 2 touchdowns on 35 carries. He finished with 351 yards from scrimmage in the win.

That overtook the 229 rushing yards and 3 TDs Memphis got from running back Jaylin Carter, along with 111 receiving yards on 5 receptions by receiver Jermane Hayes.

The Black Knights (5-5, 4-3 conference) are on a three-game losing streak after a 10-6 defeat to East Carolina (7-4, 5-2) on Saturday. Prior to its bye week, Army lost to Air Force, 24-21 , at West Point.

The 2026 Army-Navy Game will be played on Dec. 12. With the upcoming 24-team College Football Playoff format, the matchup could be added to each school's schedule as a 13th game that would be played outside CFP and bowl game consideration.

articles.title: Chelsea are fragile and need to toughen up says manager Xabi Alonso after humiliating defeat to Leeds United
articles.summary: Chelsea were dismantled by Leeds United in the Premier League on Saturday at Stamford Bridge; Xabi Alonso's side have lost three of their last four league games; Chelsea are eighth in the Premier League and have been beaten at home by both Leeds and Tottenham
articles.body:
Noah Okafor's double helped Leeds to a stunning 4-1 victory, their first at Stamford Bridge since 1999, increasing the pressure on Alonso, whose team have lost three of their last four Premier League matches and slipped to eighth.

Chelsea took the lead through Emmanuel Emegha after Moises Caicedo went off injured, but once Leeds deservedly equalised through Noah Okafor, the home side never looked likely to recover.

"We are in a fragile moment mentally," said Alonso. "When we receive a punch, we didn't recover that strong, that tough enough and today that was my feeling."

He added: "After the equaliser, after the change (Caicedo), we lost the momentum completely," said Alonso. "Until then, we were doing OK. We were creating, playing a lot on the pitch, we were coming out from the pressure, but from that moment they started believing and we started not believing and it changed totally.

"And after that, we never got the good feeling mentality in any moment, and we were not able to cope with the pressure, and we didn't get close to the goal, so it completely changed it.

"We need to find solutions for sure because there will be setbacks during any game and to be tougher and to be able to go through that and to know that it's still so long to play, it's something mandatory in this competition."

Calvert-Lewin said Chelsea "couldn't handle" Leeds' intensity with the visitors outrunning their opponents by 6km, putting in more high-speed runs and further sprinting distance.

"I try to find football solutions as well," said Alonso when asked how he will attempt to fix being bullied by teams.

"That's our job, to try to find solutions, to work on that, to create that, to have bad experiences like today and hopefully we will have good ones when we can overcome, even during the game, a difficult moment because this is football and for sure that will happen.

"But in the progression, in the process that I often talk about, this is a very, very important topic."

Chelsea won more duels but Leeds' press won them possession nine times in the final third to the hosts' one.

"There were moments that we were not competing at the level required and we need to know that that's mandatory in this competition because you will face teams with that demand again," added Alonso.

"The physicality, the duels, that is not the only explanation. I said that yesterday and I repeat that. We could do that better in a football way, not giving a ball away, trying to progress a little bit more, choosing better options. That's the solution as well but the physical part and the mentality part we can do better."

Chelsea have lost at home to both rivals Leeds and Tottenham for the first time in 67 years, upsetting supporters, who booed their team off at Stamford Bridge.

Alonso said: "I understand the disappointment for sure and we share that with them and whatever we can do is work, try to give our best to turn it back and to do much better."

articles.title: El Arsenal se enreda en Newcastle... y el City respira
articles.standfirst: Un empate que mantiene las distancias entre 'gunners' y 'sky blues'
articles.summary: Un empate que mantiene las distancias entre 'gunners' y 'sky blues'
articles.body: Tras cinco victorias consecutivas en Premier League, el Arsenal de Arteta vio cortada su buena racha en el norte, ante el Newcastle. Los vigentes campeones de Inglaterra empataron (2-2) ante un gran equipo local... con la sensación de que 'salvaron' un punto más que perder dos. El City de Maresca, mientras, se queda a seis puntos (también empató, 1-1 ante el Fulham) y es el Brighton el que, si gana esta jornada, podría ponerse a tres del liderato. El Arsenal tenía claro que una victoria hoy allanaba el camino hacia una nueva Premier League, la segunda consecutiva. El empate del City ante el Fulham abría el camino... y los de Arteta lo empezaron aprovechando con el 0-1 de Eze pasada la media hora. Un gol fantástico después de un pase brillante de Havertz a la espalda de la defensa que finalizaba, con un remate precioso, el ex del Palace. Pero el partido, pese a que se ponía claramente del lado londinense, cambió en la segunda parte. Y al Arsenal le hicieron daño en situaciones poco comunes: Odegaard erró un despeje tras la buena presión 'magpie' y Barnes definió en una rápida transición después de un buen pase de Osula. 13 minutos después del empate, tras un saque de esquina en una jugada llena de rebotes, Malick Thiaw metía la pierna y remontaba. La dinámica se confirmaba con goles: la segunda parte era clara de los locales e, incluso, el 3-1 se rondaba. Havertz, en un mal despeje de cabeza, mandó el balón al larguero de su propia portería. A Arteta, además, le crecían los problemas: David Raya se lesionaba en el hombro en un choque y tenía que ser reemplazado por Kepa. Pero el fútbol es impredecible y Madueke, en el primer disparo a puerta del Arsenal en el segundo tiempo, se inventó una gran jugada para empatar y dar aire a los 'gunners'. Fue el único remate visitante en un segundo tiempo donde, claramente, no se vio la mejor versión del vigente campeón de la Premier League. Ni los nueve minutos de añadido dieron un poco de margen a un Arsenal que 'pinchó' en el norte de Inglaterra. El City, pese a su mala racha, sigue a 'solamente' seis puntos.

articles.title: Arsenal escape with 2-2 draw at Newcastle after 'complacent' second half almost proves costly for defending champions
articles.summary: Arsenal were completely dominant in the first half at Newcastle but saw their 1-0 lead turn into a 2-1 deficit before Noni Madueke rescued a point against their re-energised hosts; Mikel Arteta called the result "two points dropped" and revealed key lesson required to take "next step"
articles.body:
Noni Madueke's equaliser at least rescued a point, but after completely dominating the first half at St James' Park Mikel Arteta says his team have learnt a harsh lesson about the need to deliver a complete performance in the Premier League.

Credit has to go to Newcastle, who were energised by Matthias Jaissle's triple substitution at half-time, with Tino Livramento, Jacob Ramsey and Anthony Elanga bringing intensity. Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw brought the goals. But the Premier League champions were their own worst enemy and, in the end, were fortunate to get away with their lead at the top of the table improved - for now.

With Man City dropping points again on Saturday and surprise-package Brighton still to play on Sunday, Arsenal remain firmly in the box seat. But Arteta is eager to drive even higher standards in his squad this season as he builds on last year's success - and he was far from impressed with how his team allowed Newcastle back into the game.

"My feeling is that we lost two points today," he told Sky Sports . "We were exceptional in the first half. At every level. Our intensity, the clarity that we have, how to attack the jumps of Newcastle every time they wanted to go man-to-man, the composure that we have, the way we use our relationship to break their press...

"It should have been 2-0, 3-0 or 4-0 up. But it wasn't. And when it wasn't, then we expected in the second half that we have to again raise the level because the opponent is going to have a reaction. The opponent did have a reaction and we were very below the level that is required to stretch the gap in a game like this in this stadium. And then we gave them belief.

"I say we give them belief because we give them a goal, we give them a throw-in that we just give them the ball. We have no structure to control the opposite winger. We concede a goal and it's game on.

"And from that it became a very chaotic game. Every set-piece, we know that they are exceptional at it and we concede from a set-piece.

"And then you have to react. Then we went back to the exceptional team that we were in the first half again for another 25 minutes and we scored a great goal. We create infinity of openings to create and score the third goal, but we lack some time or to be precise, to make that count."

The stats paint a clear picture of how different the two halves from Arsenal's perspective were. Attacking stats and, significantly, duel success numbers shifted.

Sky Sports pundit Jamie Redknapp said: "I think in the second half Arsenal were just complacent. I think they thought this was so easy and that can happen sometimes in a game.

"You're getting so much time on the ball. Declan Rice was able to turn. Bruno Guimaraes had so much time in the first half and then all of a sudden [Jacob] Ramsey comes on and he's all over you. He's closing you down. Myles Lewis-Skelly's getting under pressure and that was a full credit to Newcastle.

"The fundamentals that you have to do to win a football match by winning second balls, by putting teams under pressure, by getting in people's faces, Newcastle did well in the second half."

For former Arsenal striker Ian Wright, there is also an issue in the construction of Arsenal's midfield.

"What's worrying for me and probably for Arsenal fans is that that period where we seem to can't get it back, can't grasp it back," he said.

"I think [Newcastle] could have maybe nicked another one while it was 2-1, but they didn't. I'm very concerned with the Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes midfield. It just didn't feel in that moment that we were able to keep them off us."

He added: "It was worrying to see Arsenal collapse like they did, for the time that they did."

An injury to goalkeeper David Raya presents another problem.

Goalscorer Madueke made a point of noting the "character" Arsenal showed to get back into the game after the turnaround from 1-0 to 2-1. On reasons for the poor start to the second half he said: "Not sticking by our own principles. I don't know whether we came out too relaxed after the first half performance."

The quality of that first half performance shouldn't be overlooked. Nor should Newcastle's role in changing the game.

But clearly Arteta will zone in on that second 45 and use it as an example of how he can raise further the levels of the English champions.

"I think individually we have some top performances for 70 minutes," said Arteta. "But at this level it's not enough. At this level requires 96 [minutes] unless you score three or four goals and then you can allow yourself for 15 or 20 minutes not to be at your best.

"That's the next step this team has to make."

'Full respect' - Newcastle and Jaissle praised for turnaround

"I think first half for any player in that Newcastle team, even in that dressing room, that would have been a lonely place because you were getting played off the park, the spaces seemed so big, your home crowd have been booing you. You're like, 'this is going to be a really tough half'.

"He made three great changes. Elanga added pace, Livramento good energy down that right-hand side, and Ramsey was one of the best players on the pitch.

"Newcastle, full respect from me, and I thought they showed a great deal of effort and they played against a very difficult side in Arsenal, but they got after them. It just shows you what a bit of energy can do.

"And once that crowd get up and you get that first goal, anything was possible. And they'll look at that second half thinking, actually, we could have won this game. Really good performance from Newcastle.

"I would give Jaissle more credit because he's taken a lot of stick. It's been really hard for him, but he's definitely got some money in the bank tonight.

"He'll be proud of his team. The fans will be proud of their team. And they made it very difficult for Arsenal that second half."

articles.title: González Fuertes responde a Florentino Pérez: "A lo mejor los árbitros tienen que estar indignados con Real Madrid TV"
articles.standfirst: El analista arbitral de Radio MARCA reaccionó a las declaraciones del presidente del Madrid
articles.summary: El analista arbitral de Radio MARCA reaccionó a las declaraciones del presidente del Madrid
articles.body: Pablo González Fuertes, exárbitro y analista de 'Marcador', contestó en directo al presidente del Real Madrid después de escuchar sus palabras durante la Asamblea General Ordinaria de socios compromisarios del club blanco, celebrada este sábado 21 de noviembre en la Ciudad Real Madrid. El máximo dirigente madridista situó el caso Negreira en el centro de su discurso y cuestionó la relación entre el colectivo arbitral y el conjunto blanco. Florentino aseguró que actualmente hay 21 colegiados en Primera División, incluidos los integrantes del VAR, que fueron ascendidos durante la etapa de Negreira en el Comité Técnico de Árbitros. Además, criticó que algunos de ellos hubiesen denunciado al Real Madrid y posteriormente fueran designados para dirigir sus encuentros. «Hay un grupo de estos árbitros que han denunciado al Real Madrid. Es decir, nos denuncian y luego son asignados para arbitrar los partidos de nuestro equipo», manifestó el presidente durante su intervención. 'Marcador' recuperó esas declaraciones durante el programa y puso el fragmento a González Fuertes, que fue uno de los fundadores del sindicato arbitral al que hizo referencia la intervención de Florentino. El excolegiado no esquivó ninguna de las dos cuestiones planteadas por el presidente madridista y respondió: «Bueno, primero, que es falso que Enrique Negreira ascendiera a ningún árbitro. Punto número uno», comenzó señalando González Fuertes. «El que denunció los vídeos de Real Madrid Televisión fue el sindicato que representa a todos y cada uno de los árbitros y árbitras del fútbol profesional de este país», explicó. «Si el señor Florentino Pérez está tan indignado porque hay árbitros que le arbitren que lo denuncian, pues a lo mejor los árbitros tienen que estar indignados porque Real Madrid Televisión hace vídeos contra el colectivo arbitral semanalmente», concluyó.

articles.title: Ohio State's CFP Hopes Crushed by Nebraska, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Jeremiah Smith, More
articles.summary: The little hope that the Ohio State Buckeyes had remaining to make the College Football Playoff was crushed by the Nebraska Cornhuskers on Saturday.
articles.body:
The little hope that the Ohio State Buckeyes had remaining to make the College Football Playoff was crushed by the Nebraska Cornhuskers on Saturday.

Ryan Day's Buckeyes suffered their fourth loss of the college football regular season by a 31-28 score despite another terrific performance from Jeremiah Smith.

Smith added to his Heisman Trophy campaign with 165 receiving yards and two touchdowns.

Nebraska quarterback Anthony Colandrea was the most impactful player on the field inside Memorial Stadium.

Colandrea led the Huskers to three consecutive touchdowns in the first half to open up a 14-point advantage over the Buckeyes.

The Huskers quarterback threw for one more touchdown in the fourth quarter and then sealed the victory with a third-down run with a minute left.

Ohio State got on the board first thanks to Smith, who connected with Luke Fahey on a 67-yard touchdown pass.

Smith scored again at the end of the first half to cut the Nebraska lead to seven points after two quarters.

The Buckeyes did tie the game at 21-21 after a Bo Jackson touchdown run, but they played from behind for most of the fourth quarter.

The key turnover for Nebraska occurred in the fourth quarter, when Fahey was intercepted on a ball down the sideline that was intended for Smith.

Smith was easily Ohio State's best player on offense on Saturday, but like in other defeats, the Buckeyes experienced plenty of issues moving the ball on certain drives.

Ohio State can salvage its season a bit with a rivalry win over the Michigan Wolverines next Saturday.

Smith is still in the running for the Heisman Trophy, but that's about the only positive regarding the Buckeyes season at the moment.

articles.title: Deion Sanders, Colorado No Longer Bowl Eligible After Loss to Cincinnati, Final Box Score Stats
articles.summary: Cincinnati running back Cole Tabb tallied four touchdowns and 230 yards from scrimmage en route to a 35-28 home win over the Colorado Buffaloes on Saturday afternoon.
articles.body:
Cincinnati running back Cole Tabb tallied four touchdowns and 230 yards from scrimmage en route to a 35-28 home win over the Colorado Buffaloes on Saturday afternoon.

The Bearcats, who were a 2.5-point favorite at FanDuel Sportsbook , moved to 6-5 overall (3-5 in Big 12) and are now bowl eligible. Head coach Deion Sanders' Buffaloes dropped to 4-7 (2-6 Big 12) and are no longer bowl eligible .

Tabb's touchdowns came in a variety of ways: on one-yard runs in the first and third quarters, a 22-yard reception in the second quarter and a 50-yard catch in the third quarter.

Tabb, who now has 1,466 all-purpose yards and 18 touchdowns on the season, gave Cincinnati a 35-21 lead (following the PAT) with 2:59 remaining in the third quarter following his fourth score.

Cincinnati quarterback J.C. French IV, who fired just one incomplete pass in 19 attempts, accounted for the Bearcats' other TD on a one-yard run late in the first quarter. He threw for 10.9 yards per attempt.

On the other sideline, Colorado quarterback Isaac Wilson had an up-and-down day. He threw for 316 yards and three touchdowns on just 16 completions (12.0 yards per attempt overall). The TD passes were to Ernest Campbell for 36 yards in the first quarter, DeAndre Moore Jr. for 50 yards and Joseph Williams for 70 yards in the third quarter.

Colorado's other TD was courtesy of Richard Young from four yards out in the second quarter.

However, Wilson also threw three interceptions. MJ Cannon, Kenny Worthy and Jasper Beeler came away with the picks.

The last interception, via Worthy on the Buffaloes' 42-yard line, ended Colorado's last-gasp, desperation drive in the final minute.

Ultimately, Tabb's tremendous performance, French's efficiency and the takeaway difference (4-1 in favor of the Bearcats) turned out to be the difference.

Cincinnati and Colorado both end their regular seasons on Saturday. Cincinnati will visit BYU at 3:30 p.m. ET, and Colorado will host UCF at 2 p.m.

articles.title: United States reportedly set to host Copa América for third time in 2028
articles.summary: Argentina has won the past two competitions, including in 2024 when the U.S. last played host.
articles.body:
Copa América is set to be hosted by the United States for the third time when the tournament commences in the summer of 2028, according The Athletic's Adam Crafton .

CONMEBOL, the governing body of South American soccer, has been in discussions with Concacaf, which runs the sport in North America, Central America and the Caribbean, since 2025. The quadrennial competition, which first took place in 1916, has been held in South America except on two previous occasions — 2016 and 2024 , when it took place in the U.S.

There are 10 countries that make up CONMEBOL, but the tournament regularly invites other nations to participate. The 2024 edition featured six guest teams, all from Concacaf, including the U.S. men's national team.

There will reportedly be a qualification process for Concacaf teams, but those details, including how many guest teams will complete the final list of participants, is still to be announced.

The start date for 2028 Copa América has also yet to be announced. That summer the U.S. will also host the Olympics, which will begin in Los Angeles on July 14. Copa América 2024 took place from June 20 to July 14.

The USMNT has taken part in five Copa Américas with their best showings coming in 1995 and 2016 with a pair of fourth-place finishes. In 2024, the team failed to advance out of the group stage after winning only one of their three matches.

A week after their early exit, head coach Gregg Berhalter was fired. Two months later, Mauricio Pochettino was hired as his replacement.

Copa América 2028 will be the latest international soccer tournament hosted by the U.S. following the 2025 Club World Cup and 2026 World Cup. The U.S. is also poised to co-host the 2031 Women's World Cup along with Mexico, Jamaica and Costa Rica.

Argentina has won the previous two Copa América tournaments .

articles.title: Bill Belichick, UNC vs. UVA Final Box Score, Top Player Stats and Highlights
articles.summary: The Virginia Cavaliers achieved bowl eligibility with a 41-24 win over the ACC rival North Carolina Tar Heels at Scott Stadium in Charlottesville, Virginia, on Saturday.
articles.body:
The Virginia Cavaliers achieved bowl eligibility with a 41-24 win over the ACC rival North Carolina Tar Heels at Scott Stadium in Charlottesville, Virginia, on Saturday.

Led by head coach Bill Belichick, UNC entered the game as 1.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , but that was before clarity was gained regarding the Tar Heels' quarterback situation.

While senior quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. started North Carolina's first 10 games of the season, he did not play Saturday due to an injury suffered during last week's loss to Louisville.

Buffs Drop Bowl Eligibility in Cincy Loss

Edwards was replaced by freshman Travis Burgess, who struggled at times to maintain an offensive rhythm in his first career start. Here is a look at how Burgess and all of the key offensive players for UNC and UVA fared on Saturday:

Spearheaded by senior quarterback Beau Pribula, the Virginia offense got the scoring started, as Pribula hit wide receiver Da'Shawn Martin for a 20-yard touchdown in the first quarter:

UVA's defense then put the team in position to extend the lead to 10-0 when linebacker Kam Robinson made a leaping interception on the following drive:

North Carolina got on the board for the first time about five minutes into the second quarter, finishing off a 10-play, 75-yard drive with a one-yard touchdown run by running back Kaleb Jackson:

The Cavs needed only two plays and 17 seconds to answer right back, though, with a 75-yard scoring strike from Pribula to running back Jekail Middlebrook:

After trading field goals late in the second quarter, Virginia brought a 10-point lead into halftime, which was a significant deficit for North Carolina with an inexperienced quarterback in the lineup.

Virginia forced the Tar Heels offense to turn the ball over on downs late in the third quarter, leading directly to a four-play, 57-yard drive that ended in a 24-yard touchdown pass from Pribula to running back Xavier Brown to extend the UVA lead to 17:

Following a missed field goal by UNC, the Cavaliers essentially put the game away with 11:26 left in the fourth quarter, as Pribula threw his fourth touchdown of the day on a one-yard pass to tight end Dakota Twitty, making it 34-10:

Burgess' first career touchdown came with 6:55 remaining, throwing a five-yard score to wide receiver Trech Kekahuna, followed by a successful two-point conversion:

That technically kept UNC alive, as it trailed Virginia by 16 points, but a 32-yard rushing touchdown by Virginia running back Solomon Beebe on the ensuing drive restored a three-score lead for the Cavs:

North Carolina made the score look a bit more respectable when Burgess scored a five-yard rushing touchdown just two seconds before the final whistle.

Saturday's win gave Virginia a 6-5 overall record and 4-4 ACC record on the season. It also made the Cavaliers bowl eligible for the second consecutive season under head coach Tony Elliott.

Meanwhile, North Carolina will find itself in a must-win situation in its final game of the regular season with regard to bowl eligibility.

At 5-6 overall and 2-5 in the ACC, the Tar Heels need to beat rival NC State at home next Saturday to ensure their first trip to a bowl game under Belichick.

As for Virginia, it can lock in its second straight winning season with a road win over rival Virginia Tech next Saturday.

articles.title: Ryan Day's Updated Ohio State Contract Buyout Details With HC on Hot Seat After Nebraska Loss
articles.summary: Ohio State might be one step closer to considering a costly buyout of head coach Ryan Day after a Saturday afternoon loss to Nebraska.
articles.body:
Ohio State might be one step closer to considering a costly buyout of head coach Ryan Day after a Saturday afternoon loss to Nebraska.

The Buckeyes fell to 7-4 on the season following a 31-28 loss that knocked the AP preseason No. 1 out of College Football Playoff contention.

Day is signed through the 2031 season on a $12.5 million annual salary thanks to a contract he agreed to ahead of the 2025 campaign.

The contract included a $11.5 million buyout for each year remaining in the deal, per CBS Sports' Brandon Marcello . That means it would cost Ohio State at least $57.5 million to get out of the final five years on Day's deal.

That buyout could potentially be mitigated if Day is hired by another program. Penn State last spring owed James Franklin a buyout of $49 million that dropped to $9 million after he was hired by Virginia Tech.

When asked about potential staffing changes after the loss to Nebraska, Day said the Buckeyes would wait until after next Saturday's regular season finale against visiting Michigan to make any decisions.

"When you watch a game like this, you've got a lot of things that have to change," Day said .

Day, who is just two seasons removed from a national championship, first stepped in as the Buckeyes' head coach during the 2018 season.

He took over the role on a full-time basis ahead of the 2019 campaign before leading Ohio State to the national championship game in 2020.

Four seasons later, Day led the Buckeyes to a national title in the first year of the expanded CFP.

Ohio State was eliminated from the quarterfinal of the 2025 playoff. The Buckeyes looked on track for another CFP run this fall before the team's 6-1 start to the season ended with Julian Sayin fracturing his right elbow.

Ohio State has gone 1-3 since Day turned to true freshman Luke Fahey. That stretch has featured losses to unranked USC and Nebraska, the latter of which had lost 31 straight games against AP top 25 teams heading into Saturday.

Day's career record against AP unranked opponents has now dropped to 61-4, according to ESPN's Max Olson . He boasts an 89-16 career record to go along with his 6-5 postseason slate.

The Athletic reported Ohio State spent between $49 million and $54 million on its team this season, ranking the Buckeyes as one of the most expensive rosters in college football.

Day will have at least one more game to make his case the Buckeyes' next financial move shouldn't be to spend money on his buyout when Ohio State closes out the season next Saturday against the visiting Wolverines.

articles.title: Nebraska ends 31-game losing streak against ranked opponents as it buries No. 14 Ohio State's playoff chances
articles.summary: The Buckeyes have four losses. And Nebraska has its first win over a ranked team since 2016.
articles.body:
Nebraska's infamous losing streak against ranked opponents is over. And so are Ohio State's College Football Playoff hopes.

The Cornhuskers beat a team ranked in the AP Top 25 for the first time since 2016 on Saturday with a 31-28 win over No. 14 Ohio State . Nebraska put the game away with 7:41 to go on a 26-yard TD pass from Anthony Colandrea to Quinn Clark as Clark dove over the pylon for a 2-score lead.

Since beating Oregon in Week 3 over a decade ago, Nebraska had lost 31 straight games against ranked teams after coughing up a late lead at home to Indiana earlier in the season.

"Jeremiah Smith, give him the Heisman, we doubled him," Nebraska coach Matt Rhule told Fox after the game. "But these kids won the game today."

Ohio State cut Nebraska's lead to three with 3:52 to go, but a first-down run by Colandrea just before the two-minute warning effectively ended the game before another first-down run a minute later sealed it.

Clark's TD was set up by an interception from cornerback Victor Evans III. As QB Luke Fahey tried to hit Smith between Clark and a safety, the ball deflected into the air and Clark came down with it.

Before catching the pass, Clark's right foot was out of bounds. But since his left foot had stayed inbounds — and was down when his right foot lifted off the sideline — the interception was upheld.

After the pick, Clark's TD catch came on the ninth play of a 51-yard drive that included a fourth-down conversion.

Nebraska finished the game 10-of-16 on third downs as it rushed the ball 45 times for 176 yards. Colandrea was 19-of-28 passing for 200 yards and three scores.

Even if Smith becomes Ohio State's first Heisman winner since Troy Smith in 2006 and the Buckeyes beat Michigan in Week 13, there's no way to classify Ohio State's 2026 as anything other than a disappointment.

Just look at the way offensive lineman Carson Hinzman struggled to find the words after the loss.

"It's difficult to choke down a season like this, especially being a fifth-year senior," an emotional Hinzman said.

Everything cratered for the Buckeyes when Julian Sayin suffered a right arm injury late in the win over Indiana. Since then, Ohio State is 1-3 and has gone from a 6-1 national title contender to a 7-4 team just trying to avoid a five-loss season.

It's not all QB Luke Fahey's fault, either. The true freshman was thrust into an unenviable position when he had to make his first career start on the road against USC. And it was Ohio State's defense allowing a couple of big plays in that loss to the Trojans and further getting beaten like it rarely ever is in a loss to Oregon that has been a bigger issue.

After not allowing more than 24 points in each of its first seven games of the season, Ohio State has now given up 30 or more in three of its last four games.

Smith also hasn't had much help in the passing game. He had six catches for 165 yards and two scores. At halftime, he had 117 of Ohio State's 189 total yards. Fahey finished the game 16-of-27 for 259 yards, meaning that all other Ohio State players had 10 catches for 94 yards.

You can't blame Nebraska fans in the slightest for not assuming anything when the Cornhuskers went up 10 on Clark's TD. After all, this is a team that had been tied or leading at halftime in all 10 of its previous games this season and entered Week 12 at 6-4.

Maybe, just maybe, Saturday was the confidence boost that Nebraska has been desperately needing.

The school extended Rhule after a 7-6 season in 2025 amid potential interest from Penn State. Giving a coach with a 19-19 record an extension through three seasons is rarely a good idea. Nebraska needed results in 2026.

It might be close to getting them. A win over No. 15 Iowa in Week 13 and a bowl win would give Nebraska its first nine-win season since, not-so-coincidentally, 2016. Heck, even eight wins would be the team's most successful season since then.

But there's still plenty of work to do to get there. Just ask one of those Nebraska fans.

articles.title: No. 10 BYU survives upset scare against Kansas with triple-overtime win, keeping Big 12 and CFP hopes alive
articles.summary: BYU improves to 6-2 in conference play, needing a No. 12 Texas Tech loss to enter the Big 12 title game picture.
articles.body:
No. 10 BYU took on Kansas on Saturday afternoon and the Big 12 matchup went to triple overtime — which, by rule, turned the game into a battle of alternating two-point attempts.

Kansas got the ball first in the third overtime, but quarterback Isaiah Marshall fumbled away the Jayhawks' attempt. Bear Bachmeier and BYU then had their chance, and the Cougars quarterback found wide receiver Jojo Phillips for the win.

Regulation wasn't enough for this matchup. It looked like BYU would walk off with an easy 37-yard field goal. Cougars kicker Matthias Dunn had never missed from that distance and was previously perfect on the day, but shanked the kick far left.

The game went into overtime, which began with each team getting a possession from their own 25-yard line.

The Jayhawks got the ball first in OT and made it count. BYU's defense couldn't match Kansas' Marshall, who ran for 12 yards before taking off for the 10-yard score.

BYU answered with a QB rushing touchdown as Bachmeier barely broke the plane of the end zone on a quarterback keeper for the 2-yard score.

That sent the game into second overtime, with the Cougars starting with the ball.

BYU running back LJ Martin put the team on his back in that stanza. He took a direct snap, ran 11 yards and dove into the end zone for the go-ahead TD. The Cougars had to go for two by rule, but Bachmeier's pass was tipped and fell incomplete.

Kansas then got the ball back, needing at least a touchdown to keep the game alive.

The Jayhawks were down to their final play. On fourth-and-5, Marshall floated a ball into the end zone, and wide receiver Nahzae Cox made the contested catch. After Kansas didn't convert the two-point try, the game went into a triple overtime, where BYU won.

BYU improves to 9-2 overall with a 6-2 record in conference play. The Cougars are currently on the outside looking in for the Big 12 conference championship game, but they're still alive.

articles.title: David Raya injury: Goalkeeper taken off during Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal
articles.summary: Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya is set to have a scan on his shoulder after going off injured during Saturday's 2-2 draw with Newcastle.
articles.body:
Injuries are never good news, but Arsenal 's latest one to first-choice goalkeeper David Raya has come in the worst possible position.

The 31-year-old was forced to leave the pitch 70 minutes into Saturday's 2-2 draw with Newcastle , appearing to hurt his shoulder in an innocuous challenge with Magpies forward William Osula.

The Gunners arguably have the best depth in the league with at least two quality options in all outfield positions after a period of squad strengthening.

In goal, however, cover appears much thinner.

Raya was a key component in Arsenal 's Premier League title-winning campaign last season, was named in the Fifpro Men's World 11 and was unlucky to not win the Yashin Trophy, awarded to the world's best goalkeeper, which went to Spain team-mate Unai Simon.

Behind him, Kepa Arrizabalaga still holds the record as the most expensive goalkeeper in football history following his £72m move from Athletic Bilbao to Chelsea in August 2018, but is far behind Raya in terms of quality.

Raya's passing range and ability on the ball are key to how Arsenal build their attacks, and his presence is a big reason why they have the best defence in the league.

They have conceded just seven Premier League goals this season, with only Brighton able to match that tally - having played a game fewer.

Arsenal also brought in former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier on a free transfer in the summer but his only appearance this season came in the embarrassing Carabao Cup defeat by League Two Fleetwood.

When asked about Raya's injury, Arteta said he did not know how severe the issue is.

"Well, unfortunately, he had to come off, which is never good news," said Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta.

"He will get assessed now, and probably he will have an MRI [scan] tomorrow to see what it is exactly he has done.

"I don't know how it happened, and what the injury is at the moment, so we'll have to wait and see tomorrow."

Who was 'a consistent threat'? Newcastle v Arsenal player ratings

'Raya the one player Arsenal can't afford to lose'

Arsenal are about to enter a gruelling period of games - with or without Raya.

In the next four weeks, they face Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City , Brentford , Tottenham Hotspur and Real Madrid.

"The one player that Arsenal cannot afford to lose is David Raya," said former England forward Alan Shearer, who is a pundit on Saturday's BBC Match of the Day. "He has made such a difference since joining from Brentford in 2023.

"They have top-class cover in just about every other position but he is the one individual that Mikel Arteta will be thinking 'we don't want to play without him for an extended period'. They could, of course go into the transfer market if they need to in January, but Arteta will be desperately hoping Raya is not out for long."

Raya is reportedly close to agreeing a new deal at the club, which shows his importance to the Gunners with two years remaining on his contract.

Ex-England midfielder Jamie Redknapp said on Sky Sports that Raya is "irreplaceable".

"Kepa is not up to the level of him - I actually think he struggles in the Premier League," added Redknapp. "Obviously we've seen in the Carabao Cup last year in the final.

"He is now going to have to play some games and that's going to be difficult for him.

"It will change everything for Arsenal for a while so that's a massive blow depending on how long David Raya is out because he is irreplaceable - probably the best goalkeeper in the Premier League, if not one of the best in the world."

articles.title: Conexión letal de la 'BMV' para desatar al Madrid
articles.standfirst: Bellingham firmó el 1-1 en el minuto 66 tras una gran jugada coral del tridente blanco
articles.summary: Bellingham firmó el 1-1 en el minuto 66 tras una gran jugada coral del tridente blanco
articles.body: Con el Madrid contra las cuerdas, la 'BMV' saltó al rescate con una conexión letal que volvió a despertar a un Bernabéu casi anestesiado por el juego blanco frente al Celta. Y todo arrancó con una gran parada de Courtois... y en las botas de Vinicius, que había entrado al poco de empezar la segunda parte. El brasileño agarró el balón en banda izquierda y con muchos metros por recorrer, unos que tuvo que realizar con el runrún de la grada. Unas pérdidas innecesarias minutos antes empezaban a dibujar otro escenario tenso para el 7, que volvió al césped del Bernabéu en Liga tras la sanción de cuatro partidos. Pero Vinicius ni se lo pensó. Arrancó la motocicleta para iniciar la transición blanca, llega hasta la frontal del área y conecta con Mbappé, que se la deja de cara a Bellingham para que empale a Radu con con un tiro seco y potente abajo. Minutos 66 y 1-1 en el marcador gracias al sexto gol de Bellingham en esta temporada tras la cuarta asistencia de Mbappé. La conexión entre los tres volvió a demostrar el potencial ofensivo del tridente blanco, capaz de resolver una jugada en apenas unos segundos. Un tridente trata de recuperar Mourinho... suministrando los minutos del brasileño para que vaya recuperando la confianza en su fútbol. Vinicius puso la velocidad y la conducción, Mbappé aportó la pausa y la visión para encontrar al inglés y Bellingham se encargó de poner el broche con un remate preciso. Una acción que permitió al Madrid recuperar el pulso del partido y encender de nuevo al Bernabéu.

El equipo comandado por el técnico portugués Leonardo Jardim necesitaba al menos un empate a domicilio para levantar el título y lo consiguió ante un rival dirigido por el también portugués Abel Ferreira, que abrió el marcador en el minuto 11 con un cabezazo del colombiano Jhon Arias. Con el empate, el conjunto carioca sumó 80 puntos y, a falta de dos jornadas para el final del torneo, quedó fuera del alcance del Palmeiras, el único que amenazaba el título y al que dejó a seis puntos de diferencia (74).

articles.title: Motherwell 1-2 Rangers: Ryan Naderi strikes late to snatch Scottish Premiership victory at Fir Park
articles.summary: Report as Rangers score a late winner against Motherwell; Emmanuel Fernandez opened the scoring; Jake Girdwood-Reich pulled the hosts level; Ryan Naderi's late deflected strike secured the win for Rangers to cut Celtic's Premiership lead back to four points
articles.body:
After Celtic's impressive 4-1 win against St Mirren, Rangers knew a win was vital to remain within touching distance of their Old Firm rivals at the top of the table.

Emmanuel Fernandez gave them the perfect start, nodding in from a corner to put them in front at Fir Park.

But Jake Girdwood-Reich struck his first Motherwell goal against the run of play before the break.

Rangers had 29 shots at goal in total but found Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen in top form and the New Zealand international pulled off one of the saves of the season to deny Dujon Sterling with five minutes left.

But they were undone late on when Naderi's shot from eight yards went in off Martin Moorman after the Austrian had blocked a shot from Badredine Bouanani.

It handed Rangers their first win at Fir Park for three years to remain four points behind Celtic ahead of their game in hand against Aberdeen on Tuesday, live on Sky Sports .

Motherwell - who had been unbeaten in three - remain 10th.

8: GOAL RANGERS! In comes the corner and Emmanuel Fernandez manages to push away his defender before rising up and nodding home.

11: SAVE! OFF THE LINE! Djeidi Gassama's strike from range is pushed away well by Alex Paulsen, with Ryan Naderi's rebound cleared by Martin Moormann.

15: Another corner for Rangers as they come at Motherwell relentlessly, but the hosts manage to clear.

21: ALMOST! Big clearance from Dujon Sterling after a really good break from Motherwell.

21: GOAL MOTHERWELL! Tom Sparrow sends in Motherwell's first cross and Jake Girdwood-Reich volleys home.

29: HUGE CHALLENGE! Seb Palmer-Houlden looks to be through, but it's a brilliantly timed tackle from Fernandez that puts the ball out for a Motherwell corner.

41: SAVE! An absolutely sublime touch from Naderi to take the ball around Girdwood-Reich only to see it palmed away by Paulsen.

59: OFF THE POST! Almost a Motherwell own-goal as Sparrow turns Tuur Rommens' low ball onto the post.

74: SAVE! Rangers' first corner of the second half is punched clear by Paulsen.

85: WHAT A SAVE! Paulsen somehow gets a hand to Sterling's effort to push it onto the crossbar.

88: GOAL RANGERS! Naderi's strike takes a deflection off Moormann and it's in the net.

Former Rangers and Motherwell midfielder Andy Halliday on Sky Sports:

"That's such a massive win for Rangers. You look at the next six games, five of them are at Ibrox so it's so important for them to keep the pressure on Celtic at the top end of the table.

"From a Motherwell point of view, I feel for Martin Moormann because I thought him and Paulsen were the reason it was 1-1 for so long.

"Take nothing away from Rangers, they were terrific and the introduction of Findlay Curtis changed the game.

"He was so direct, so positive, put so many crosses into the box. He's bided his time all season and he was excellent.

"Rangers kept asking questions of Motherwell. Ryan Naderi was pivotal again.

"He always puts himself about and his work rate is incredible.

"He might not be cleanest and he might look untidy at times, but nobody can fault his work rate.

"Derek McInnes said the most important thing was to leave with three points and that's exactly what Rangers have done."

Rangers manager Derek McInnes speaking to Sky Sports:

"A first-class performance. We were really strong throughout. Very rarely can you go away from home in the Scottish Premiership and have so much dominance, but with that dominance there has to be more authority in the game, more control of the game in terms of scoring goals and taking the game away from the opponent.

"We were a bit unfortunate, we conceded the corner with a wee deflection.

"They get the break in, they get the corner, and then we were just so sloppy. One of our players isn't doing his job, picking up when he should have been. It could have cost us, but we made the game.

"Again, it's disappointing that we had to wait to the very end, but when it comes it's a great moment for us. A last-minute winner is always so brilliant to get and to do it in front of our supporters made it special because they were brilliant back and forth the whole night.

"We've all been around football enough to know that those last-minute ones are kind of systematic with a team who are successful, so hopefully that is the case.

"The difference between that one point and three points is obviously clearly important to us."

articles.title: El Heliodoro se queda sin goles
articles.standfirst: El Tenerife suma su sexta jornada sin perder y el Mallorca alcanza la séptima sin conocer la derrota
articles.summary: El Tenerife suma su sexta jornada sin perder y el Mallorca alcanza la séptima sin conocer la derrota
articles.body: Tenerife y Mallorca igualaron a todo en el Heliodoro en una cita sin goles que deja a los blanquiazules con su sexta jornada sin perder y a los bermellones con la séptima sin conocer la derrota. El primer tiempo discurrió por la senda de la igualdad. Ninguno de los dos equipos se dio una tregua. Bajar un balón al césped significaba estar rodeado de contrarios y la única manera de que el esférico circulase era con pases de seguridad. Los locales le pusieron más voluntad y empujaron al Mallorca hacia su área, pero ninguno fue capaz de crear situaciones que generasen peligro alguno. Ni siquiera a través de las jugadas a balón parado. La pizarra se impuso al talento y los duelos individuales afloraron más que la creatividad en un campo de minas que solo se desactivó cuando el árbitro señaló el descanso. Tanto Cervera como Luis García movieron sus piezas en el segundo acto, pero la cita siguió siendo tan áspera como en el primero. El Mallorca demostró por qué es el segundo equipo que menos encaja en Segunda y apenas dejó resquicio para el error. El único fue en el minuto 56 y Tenas estuvo muy hábil para achicar espacio y generar que el disparo de Enric Gallego impactase en su pecho. Adri Fuentes, una pesadilla para cualquier central cuando logra girarse y enfoca la portería, dio la réplica en el 72 con un latigazo que Dani Martín desvío a córner con una gran estirada. Y para que el encuentro tuviese también algo de pimienta el Heliodoro protestó una caída en el área visitante del canterano Dani Fernández que ni el árbitro, ni el VAR estimaron punible por más que lo pareciese en directo. Eso sí, Tenas salvó a su equipo con una parada antológica a disparo de Nacho Gil en el minuto 93.

articles.title: Austin Mack Impresses in Place of Keelon Russell, Box Score Stats, Highlights from Alabama's Win
articles.summary: Austin Mack led the Alabama Crimson Tide to a 47-0 shutout victory over the Chattanooga Mocs at home Saturday, throwing four touchdown passes.
articles.body:
Austin Mack led the Alabama Crimson Tide to a 47-0 shutout victory over the Chattanooga Mocs at home Saturday, throwing four touchdown passes.

The Crimson Tide entered the matchup as 48.5-point favorites over the Mocs, per FanDuel Sportsbook .

Biggest 5-Star Recruiting Busts of Past Decade 👎

In his first career start, Mack threw for 254 yards with an 80 percent completion rate and four touchdown passes, stepping in as the starter for Keelon Russell, who was ruled out with an ankle injury.

Alabama's defense stepped up, shutting out Chattanooga while limiting starting quarterback Parker Awad to 12 pass attempts and 59 passing yards.

The lopsided victory saw Alabama hold Chattanooga to just 86 yards of total offense while recording 553 yards of its own.

(21) South Carolina: 4-4 (CONF), 6-4 (OVR)

Alabama jumped out to a 33-0 lead at halftime, with Mack rushing for the lone touchdown in the first quarter before an explosive 24-point second quarter.

Mack connected with Ryan Coleman-Williams, Lotzeir Brooks and Rico Scott in the second, spreading the ball around to get everyone involved.

The Crimson Tide controlled the clock in the third quarter, with Mack finding Noah Rogers for his final touchdown of the game before taking a seat with a comfortable 40-point lead. Jett Thomalla stepped in to close out the game.

The freshman Thomalla connected with Kevin Riley in the fourth quarter, throwing the first touchdown pass of his career to close out the 47-0 win.

Alabama will host the Auburn Tigers next Saturday in its final regular-season game.

articles.title: La bendita injusticia de Mourinho
articles.standfirst: La contracrónica del Real Madrid - Celta
articles.summary: La contracrónica del Real Madrid - Celta
articles.body: El Madrid acabó con Güler y Bellingham de organizadores, jugando en la base por detrás del batallón de delanteros con el que terminó Mourinho ante el Celta. No cabían más. Endrick, Vini, Espí y Mbappé para arreglar en los últimos minutos uno de esos partidos que el Madrid podía lamentar al final de la temporada. No estaba en los planes de Mourinho, desde luego, un posible tropiezo en el Bernabéu tras su espectacular racha de ocho victorias consecutivas. Y se tiró con todo a por la novena, que llegó de la mano del de siempre en situaciones de emergencia. Mbappé, no. Espí. Carlos Espí demuestra cada vez que sale que se puede ser un ídolo jugando cinco minutos. El chico es un killer. Se mueve como pocos en el área y con sus casi dos metros derriba defensas como bolos. Letal en el cuerpo a cuerpo y en el remate, volvió a ser el salvador del Madrid. Nueve puntos le ha dado al Madrid en Liga. Tres en la Champions con el tanto de Roma. Se le volverá a preguntar a Mourinho por qué no juega más y responderá el entrenador que para qué, si con un rato es suficiente. Cuatro goles en 62 minutos esta temporada. Bendita injusticia tiene el Real Madrid. No encuentra aliados Valverde que le saquen del lateral. Porque ya no es que ni Trent ni Dumfries lleguen a su nivel cuando juegan, es que no llegan al 5. Repartió descansos Mourinho ante el Celta y se quedó en el banquillo Fede, que tuvo que salir en el 55' por Alexander-Arnold, que firmó otra triste noche como madridista. El inglés nunca fue un gran defensor, pero en el Madrid se ha hecho muy pequeño y ha quedado reducido a un jugador de buen golpeo y poco más. Y con eso en el Madrid no te da. Se plantó el Real Madrid en el Bernabéu con su espectacular racha de ocho victorias consecutivas, entre las que figuraba la conseguida en en El Clásico. Pero la afición del Madrid siempre quiere más y no dio ni 10 minutos de tregua. Se adelantó el Celta y empezó el run-run, que fue más según pasaba el tiempo sin que el Madrid empatara. Y mira que pidió Florentino en la Asamblea, con el asentimiento de Nadal, más aplausos para los jugadores, pero el Bernabéu lo tiene claro: quiere la excelencia en cada minuto. Cuando el equipo logró el empate, eso sí, el Bernabéu ya fue otro y se puso a jugar. Más que lo fallara, llamó la atención cómo. El francés pudo lograr el empate en la primera parte por medio de un penalti que él mismo provocó, pero mandó el lanzamiento por encima del larguero. Muy por encima. Amagó dos veces antes del golpeo y terminó firmando su peor penalti con la camiseta del Real Madrid. Un clásico del Bernabéu, reconocer las carreras de los grandes jugadores. Entró Aspas en el minuto 76 y se llevó una gran ovación del Santiago Bernabéu. El gallego tuvo más aplausos que Trent, por ejemplo. Y dejó su sello con su calidad. Es probable que fuera su último baile en la Castellana. Impresionante el homenaje que preparó el Real Madrid a Jesús de Miguel, con la pareja, la hermana y el padre del futbolista presentes en el césped del Santiago Bernabéu. Un homenaje que encogió el corazón de los 75.000 aficionados que acudieron al Bernabéu. Imposible aguantar las lágrimas.

articles.title: El imperdible gesto de Valverde con Vinicius que nadie vio tras el 2-1
articles.standfirst: El capitán blanco fue a buscar al brasileño para que recibiese el cariño del Bernabéu. Endrick también quiso sumarse al mensaje con un guiño al '7'
articles.summary: El capitán blanco fue a buscar al brasileño para que recibiese el cariño del Bernabéu. Endrick también quiso sumarse al mensaje con un guiño al '7'
articles.body: Cuando Carlos Espí anotó el 2-1, todas las miradas se dirigieron al goleador y a los jugadores que corrían a felicitarle. Sin embargo, hubo un detalle que pudo pasar desapercibido. Valverde, como capitán, tuvo claro que había otro protagonista al que había que poner en el centro de la celebración. Fue directo a buscar a Vinicius, lo agarró y se lo llevó con el resto de sus compañeros para que también recibiese el cariño de la grada. Un gesto de respaldo al brasileño, especialmente significativo en un momento en el que necesita sentir el apoyo del madridismo. Y es que Vini había sido uno de los grandes protagonistas del encuentro desde su entrada en el minuto 57, todavía con 0-0 en el marcador. Su impacto fue inmediato, revolucionó el ataque blanco y acabó siendo decisivo con la asistencia del gol. A ese mensaje también se sumó Endrick, que dibujó el número 7 con las manos hacia la grada mientras señalaba a su compañero. Dos gestos que hablan de la complicidad que existe dentro del vestuario y de la importancia que tiene Vinicius para sus compañeros. El mensaje es claro: el brasileño no está solo y recuperar su mejor versión es también una misión colectiva.

articles.title: Carlos Espí saca al Madrid de otro lío
articles.standfirst: El punta vuelve a anotar en el tramo final el gol del triunfo ante un Celta notable que puso en apuros a los blancos desde los cinco minutos, con gol de Durán. Bellingham brilla de nuevo
articles.summary: El punta vuelve a anotar en el tramo final el gol del triunfo ante un Celta notable que puso en apuros a los blancos desde los cinco minutos, con gol de Williot. Bellingham brilla de nuevo
articles.body: Espí. Carlos Espí. El Real Madrid invocó a su solucionador de problemas y volvió a actuar como tal. Un partido complejo, trabado, bien trabajado y defendido por el Celta, cayó del lado blanco cuando apareció el ariete para cabecear un gran centro de Vinicius, que aceptó de buen grado su papel de revulsivo. La eficacia de Espí sacó a su equipo de otro lío, como ante el Espanyol o el Elche, y mantuvo la buena racha blanca desde el Metropolitano en un partido sin mucho brillo pero efica para dejar sin premio a un Celta al que este año no le sale la moneda de cara casi nunca. Esta vez jugó bien, y no fue bastante. Costó al Bernabéu entrar en partido, después del sobrecogedor homenaje a Jesús de Miguel y su familia. Una muestra de respeto abrumadora por parte de ambos clubes, jueces y aficionados. Después de una de las ovaciones más largas y sentidas que se recuerdan, el pitido inicial descorchó al Celta, que salió mandón y aprovechó las rotaciones del Madrid. Alargó la primera posesión hasta provocar un córner, atrajo al rival a su campo y sorprendió con un pase de primeras de Ilaix cruzado, excelente. Marcó Pablo Durán, que disfruta a campo abierto en Chamartín, pero sirvió con precisión Williot Swedberg, que se consagró un año atrás en el estadio blanco. Irrumpió en el área como un turista, a espaldas de Trent, y sirvió un caramelo bajo las piernas de Huijsen. Sorpresa. Venía el Celta de Giráldez como un equipo más sólido que atrevido, cambiando el plan de pasados ejercicios. Sin ningún fichaje en el once y seis titulares formados en el Fortuna, el equipo gallego se comportó con inteligencia, cerrando espacios en defensa, prietas las filas, y desplegándose con movilidad en ataque. Incomodó a un Madrid que creyó que podría gestionar el partido sin mucho esfuerzo, con su inercia ganadora, y le costó hasta generar ocasiones. Probó Diomande pronto, con un centro que no alcanzó a rematar en plancha Bernardo, pero el equipo de Mourinho no remató entre los tres palos hasta pasada la media hora. En cambio, los gallegos generaron varias acciones de mérito, casi siempre con Williot como protagonista. La más clara, rematando al lateral de la red un centro atrás de Carreira tras jugada larga y fluida. Las más frecuentes, a la espalda de Arnold, señalado por el Bernabéu. Tan discreto estuvo el Madrid que Mou puso a calentar a medio banquillo desde el minuto 22. Faltaba movimiento, especialmente sin balón, y por eso el Celta sufría poco. Pero bastó una pelota filtrada en el área para que Mbappé sacara un penalti. Se escurrió de Javi Rodríguez, que le enganchó del brazo. Dónde vas. Penaltito, sí, pero mucho menos que el de Santander. Adrián Cordero pitó, no corrigió el VAR y Kylian se dispuso a cobrar la pieza. Ahí entendió el Bernabéu que la noche no venía fácil. El 10 remató fuerte, centrado, engañando a Radu, arriba. Nada. Pese al arreón de Bellingham, el más inspirado con la pelota, al descanso con 0-1. Cambió Giráldez tras el descanso, a Jutglà por Hugo Álvarez. Pero cambió el Madrid, que salió más agresivo. Al minuto evitó Javi Rodríguez, el gol de Carreras, que apareció por sorpresa en el área pequeña. Metió intensidad el equipo blanco, hundiendo a su adversario, aunque tampoco hacía trabajar a Radu. Así que a los diez minutos, triple cambio. Valverde, Cucurella y Vinicius. Suplente en la primera justa con Diomande de igual a igual, saltó con media hora larga para sacar rebeldía, carácter y desborde. Que falta hacían. No se puede negar que Vinicius lo intentó. Perdió las primeras. Incluso salió Mourinho a animarle cuando perdió una pelota sencilla. El caso es que el Celta se había estirado para crear dos buenas opciones, un tiro de Jutglá desde la frontal, solo y fuera, y otro duro y esquinado de Durán que sacó a pasear la mano sagrada de Courtois, y ambas sirvieron de preámbulo del empate. Persistió Vinicius con una diagonal, metió en la frontal a Mbappé que la dejó muerta y Bellingham cruzó a la red. Intratable Jude. No se puede negar que Mourinho lo puso todo para ganar. Metió primero a Endrick y después a Espí. Tampoco se achantó Giráldez, que refrescó el ataque con Driouech, Rueda y, sobre todo, con Aspas, ovacionado por la grada en su última visita al Bernabéu. Dejó un pase estupendo que no acertó a desviar en boca de gol Javi Rueda, que entró como un trueno. Perdonó el Celta que no se cerró, asumiendo riesgos, y lo pagó. En una transición salió Bellingham con elegancia, abrió a Vini y sirvió el centro templado para el cabezazo salvador de Espí. Héroe. Honor también para Junior, desequilibrante en ambos tantos para rescatar un partido complicadísimo por mérito del Celta. Pero el Madrid este año huele bien porque tiene pegada de sobra. Espí es un cañón.

articles.title: Luca Williams-Barnett: Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi compares teenager to Lamine Yamal after Ipswich heroics
articles.summary: Tottenham teenager Luca Williams-Barnett starred in Spurs' 2-0 home win over Ipswich on his first start for club; the 18-year-old scored the opener and helped set up Dominic Solanke's goal; Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi hails "special" talent and compares him to Barcelona's Lamine Yamal
articles.body:
De Zerbi turned to the highly rated Spurs academy graduate after two bright cameos and he delivered, scoring on his first Premier League start after 15 minutes before a mazy run set up Dominic Solanke at the start of the second half.

After Williams-Barnett made his senior debut at the age of 16 last season, the clamour for the teenager to play has only increased during a difficult last 12 months, and De Zerbi decided 10 days ago to include him in the starting line-up against Ipswich.

During a chat on Thursday with the skilful England U19 international, De Zerbi asked Williams-Barnett to play with freedom and work hard without the ball "like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal" before he agreed when asked if the teenager could reach similar heights.

After De Zerbi revealed Williams-Barnett prepared for the match on the team bus by watching YouTube clips of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar, he said: "Luca is a special player.

"I'm not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think. He played very well. He's lucky because he's playing in a top club with top team-mates.

"I decided to play today with Luca from 10 days and in my plan, it was [James] Maddison and Luca very close to speak the same language, to play together and the experience of Maddison I thought could be important.

"The behaviour of Maddison could help him to play with freedom. And Thursday, I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things. Just two things. To play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom.

"And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are the attackers.

"Even if they are Ballon d'Or winners, or any way the players with talent, they have to work on the pitch."

Asked if Williams-Barnett can reach the level of Lamine Yamal, De Zerbi said: "Yes, I think so.

"And one of the best things in my career… I've seen today in the bus from the training ground to the stadium, because he was very close with me, while we were coming in the stadium, he was watching on YouTube Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar.

"I thought he was a special guy, because if one hour and thirty minutes before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. The football is magic, no?"

Williams-Barnett joined Tottenham as a 10-year-old from Luton, his home town, and has been in the Spurs academy since.

There has been plenty of hype around the winger, whose talent was noticeable when he won the U18 Premier League goal of the season award for a long-range stunner against Leicester.

The teenager then began featuring in Spurs' first-team squads, but after being named on the bench for a handful of games in the 2024/25 season, Williams-Barnett was finally handed his debut in September 2025 by then-boss Thomas Frank as he came on as a substitute in the Carabao Cup third-round home win over Doncaster.

Eight days later, Williams-Barnett signed his first professional contract with Spurs at the age of 17.

His appearance against Doncaster proved to be his only first-team action last season as he hit a hat-trick against Leicester for Tottenham U21s before netting five goals in a win over Slavia Prague for Spurs' academy team in a UEFA Youth League game.

He was deservedly rewarded by De Zerbi for a fine youth season by playing a part in Tottenham's pre-season plans as he showed glimpses of his skill and quality during some run-outs.

But he has finally made his first-team breakthrough this season, and he should have had an assist on his Premier League debut in last month's win over Crystal Palace after he came on as a substitute to superbly tee up Mohammed Kudus, who somehow missed to add a third in the 2-0 win (watch below) .

Ahead of the defeat to Leeds, De Zerbi admitted Williams-Barnett was ready for a full debut, and he considered it for the win at Chelsea last month, but he was again a late second-half substitute in the loss at Elland Road.

But substitute appearances are set to no longer be an option after his stunning full debut against Ipswich.

On the international stage, Williams-Barnett has represented England at all levels between U15s and U19s to date.

In September, he came on for Arsenal sensation Max Dowman to make his England U19 debut in a 1-0 win over the Republic of Ireland.

Tottenham and Arsenal have two of England's brightest prospects, and the pair could play major parts in north London derbies in the years to come.

Solanke: You have to give Williams-Barnett assist!

Williams-Barnett was denied an assist on his full debut despite his fine work to set up Solanke's goal.

Williams-Barnett terrorised the Ipswich defence from his left-wing position to tee up the striker with a low cross for a simple 51st-minute finish.

But Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton's diversion into Solanke's path meant Williams-Barnett was not officially credited with the assist.

It meant Williams-Barnett, at the age of 18 years and 51 days, just missed out on becoming the second-youngest player to both score and assist in a Premier League game (Michael Owen in December 1997 at 17y 364d).

Solanke, however, hopes the club will appeal the assist decision.

He told Sky Sports : "No, you have to give that to him! It's just a tiny touch [from Walton]. Hopefully the club can sort that out."

He added on Williams-Barnett's display: "Luca was magnificent today.

"We see him in training every day. We know what a player he is. He's such a talent, honestly, and to see him come in and do that in his first Premier League start is crazy.

"We'll be celebrating with him today, but he can bring so much to us."

articles.title: Michigan Receiver Andrew Marsh Suspended as He Faces a Misdemeanor Charge of Indecent Exposure
articles.summary: ANN ARBOR, Mich. (AP) — Michigan receiver Andrew Marsh was suspended and scratched from the lineup against No. 4 UCLA on Saturday as he faces a misdemeanor charge of indecent exposure after a food delivery driver alleged he exposed himself to her after she dropped off his order.
articles.body:
ANN ARBOR, Mich. (AP) — Michigan receiver Andrew Marsh was suspended and scratched from the lineup against No. 4 UCLA on Saturday as he faces a misdemeanor charge of indecent exposure after a food delivery driver alleged he exposed himself to her after she dropped off his order.

"We thought it warranted a game suspension," coach Kyle Whittingham said after an 18-16 win over the Bruins in three overtimes.

Whittingham said he expects Marsh to play 16th-ranked Ohio State on the road Saturday.

Pittsfield Township Police released details of the incident Marsh was involved with in a social media post on Thursday. Marsh was charged last month by the Washtenaw County Prosecutor's Office and is set to appear for arraignment and pretrial proceedings on Dec. 2, according to police and court documents.

Police say they were contacted by the driver, who told them Marsh pulled aside a blanket and exposed his genitals to her as she turned to leave on Feb. 2. Marsh sent a message to the driver stating she was attractive and asking her to return, according to the police statement.

An 18-year-old male at the address confirmed he was the recipient of the delivery, according to police. Indecent exposure in the state can carry a prison sentence of up to one year, a fine of up to $1,000 or both.

A message sent to Marsh's lawyer seeking comment has not been returned.

Marsh, a sophomore from Texas, leads Michigan with 48 catches through 10 games. He has 459 yards and one touchdown reception in his second season with the team.

articles.title: 'They looked like a team again' - Hearts  roar back with Dundee demolition
articles.summary: After a worrying week before the international break, Hearts respond is style by thrashing Dundee 8-0 at Dens Park.
articles.body:
"I've been in football 37 years and I've never experienced anything like that," said a hugely dispirited Steven Pressley after Dundee were demolished 8-0 at home by Hearts on Saturday.

The jubilant victors can top that span of time by quite a distance given they are celebrating their biggest away win since they began playing league football in the 1890s, a result which also happens to be Dundee's record home defeat.

It was just the third 8-0 game in Scottish top-flight history, after Rangers crushed Clyde in 1931 and Celtic hammered Hamilton in 1988.

The eight at Dens Park came from 14 efforts on target and an expected goals (xG) of just 3.5.

Ruthless Hearts put eight past ramshackle 10-man Dundee

There were some fine finishes, a deft first-time effort from Sabah Kerjota being the pick of the bunch, a lot of shoddy defending, and a red card for the hosts before the hour with the score at 4-0.

Just the tonic for Hearts after three defeats in a week prior to the international break, including a League Cup semi-final derby and a shellacking from Falkirk which ended their 19-month unbeaten league streak at Tynecastle.

"They really looked like a team again," enthused former club hero John Robertson on Sportsound. "The rotations were good, the passing was good. The guys coming off the bench wanted to be part of this and they just kept going and going."

Another ex-Hearts player, Michael Stewart, called it the "perfect evening".

"To come here and win was the most important thing, but to do it in such a fashion is as good a reset as you're ever going to get," he said on Premier Sports.

'Clean sheet maybe most important thing'

Hearts are the Premiership's top scorers with 34 from 13 outings.

Add goals against and you have a whopping tally of 56, with five conceded at home to Falkirk last time and seven shipped at Celtic Park last month.

This was just a third league blank for Wouter Vrancken's defence.

"It sounds crazy after scoring eight, but the clean sheet is maybe the most important thing," added Robertson. "They just haven't had enough of them."

Reflecting on the biggest win of his career, the Belgian appeared to agree, telling BBC Sport Scotland: "What actually pleased me the most was at six or seven when Dundee were countering, nine players were sprinting back to fight for a clean sheet.

Hearts returned from the previous international break with a 5-0 win over St Mirren before the heavy loss to Celtic and Vrancken is certainly not getting carried away with nine more games coming over the next 30 days, beginning at home to Monaco in the Conference League on Thursday.

"We had talks before our days off, they were really honest and open," he revealed.

"It was good to hear but you have to take ownership of it on the pitch. You can talk as much as you want but if you can't show it on the pitch it doesn't mean anything.

"When you do it like this it's the first step. But it's only the first step, only one game and we have to try to bring more.

"It was ruthless but the schedule is also ruthless – but we got a good boost from tonight."

Having gone into the international break on the back off those three successive losses, Hearts fans may have been apprehensive.

After all, Dundee had lost just once at Dens Park all season, back in August.

However, the hosts were abject, allowing Hearts so much room.

"Every aspect of our performance was below par," bemoaned Pressley. "We looked unmotivated and lacking edge.

"Of course the sending off made the second half very difficult, but we didn't do the things that are normally associated with our performance.

"We weren't gritty enough in our defending, we didn't fill the spaces we normally do. We normally defend in a particularly strong manner, but we didn't do that.

"I can only apologise. My thoughts are that it's on myself. It's my responsibility to make sure you see a motivated Dundee team, it is my responsibility to make sure we are tactically sound, it is my responsibility to make sure they show grit and determination and not go under like we did.

"I had a little sense we haven't been quite on it over the last couple of weeks but I never expected that and I take ownership."
