articles.title: Carlos Espí: "Estaba agachado porque me estaban dando por todos lados"
articles.standfirst: El delantero habló en zona mixta tras regalarle los tres puntos al Real Madrid
articles.summary: El delantero habló en zona mixta tras regalarle los tres puntos al Real Madrid
articles.body: Carlos Espí lo volvió hacer. El delantero español, que lleva cuatro goles en 63 minutos de juego, regaló los tres puntos al Real Madrid tras firmar otro tanto en los minutos finales. En la celebración, donde recibió por todos lados, se sintió la unión de un vestuario que no para de crecer... y que cada vez está más unido. Primer gol en el Bernabéu: “Yo creo que es el más especial. Se me han dado muchos días en meter aquí, en el Bernabéu, con todos los madridistas, y la verdad que es un día que no voy a olvidar”. Entrada desde el banquillo: “Hoy ha sido un partido complicado. Como tú dices, cada jugador que ha salido del banquillo ha ayudado, ha aportado, y yo he salido y le voy a dar el máximo por este club y por la afición”. Fórmula para ser decisivo en pocos minutos: “Estar preparado, trabajar cada día para estar preparado, como he dicho, para no tocarme del míster, sean 5, sean 10, sean 30. Estar preparado para tener la ayuda del equipo, como hoy, y muy contento”. Su encuentro con Rafa Nadal: “La verdad, si te digo la verdad, lo he pasado a ver ahí, estaba muy orgulloso de mí, una leyenda como Rafa Nadal, que estar ahí presente, hablando conmigo, ha sido muy contento por eso y muy feliz”. Deseo de tener más minutos: “Yo trabajo cada día para tener más minutos, creo que todo jugador quiere jugar más. Estoy muy contento por lo que ha dado Mourinho y voy a dar el máximo”. Celebración de su gol: “Como he dicho al principio, es un día soñado. No sabes las veces que lo he soñado con meter aquí, cerrar con toda la afición y encima que te coreen. Ha sido muy especial y muy contento”. Cariño del vestuario y de Mourinho: “Bueno, ojalá sea así siempre. Están muy contentos todos, en el vestuario están todos muy felices por mí. Mourinho también está eufórico, muy contento y hay que seguir adelante”. Las palabras de Mourinho tras el gol: “Está eufórico, gritando y estamos hablando un poco y muy contentos por mí y por la victoria”. 12. Las collejas de sus compañeros en la celebración: “Sí, somos toda una familia. Se ha visto en la celebración. La verdad es que estaba agachado porque me estaban dando por todos lados. Y ver todos los banquillos que han ido conmigo y todo el equipo, yo estoy muy contento”.

articles.title: Fernando Sanz tiene claro lo que ocurre con Espí: "Es lo que encanta a la afición del Madrid"
articles.standfirst: El tertuliano de 'Marcador' destacó la actuación del delantero
articles.summary: El tertuliano de 'Marcador' destacó la actuación del delantero
articles.body: El Real Madrid volvió a necesitar una remontada para sacar adelante un partido que se le había complicado más de lo previsto. El conjunto de José Mourinho terminó imponiéndose por 2-1 al Celta en el Santiago Bernabéu, gracias a los tantos de Jude Bellingham y Carlos Espí, este último a cinco minutos del final. Los de Giráldez se habían adelantado por medio de Pablo Durán y habían conseguido marcharse al descanso con ventaja. En 'Marcador', Fernando Sanz valoró el rendimiento del equipo blanco y puso el foco en dos futbolistas que cambiaron la dinámica del encuentro: Vinicius y, especialmente, Carlos Espí. El tertuliano reconoció que el Real Madrid había firmado una actuación discreta, pero encontró motivos para el optimismo en la aportación de ambos desde el banquillo. «Partido flojo del Real Madrid, partido de los que vimos a principio de temporada y que nos desesperaba, pero muy positivo en la entrada de Vinicius y, sobre todo, en la entrada de Espí», señaló. Espí ingresó en el terreno de juego en el minuto 79 y terminó resolviendo el encuentro con el tanto del 2-1 en el 85. «Es un jugador que, después de lo de hoy, se merece muchos más minutos de los que está disputando. Yo creo que es un jugador que podría hacer muchísimos goles en el Real Madrid, que de hecho los va a hacer», afirmó. El tertuliano destacó especialmente una acción de lucha durante un tiro de esquina, un detalle que considera representativo de la personalidad del futbolista. «Esa lucha, ese sacrificio, ese punto de honor, ese juego en equipo, esa humildad, yo creo que son las características de un jugador del Real Madrid», explicó. Sanz insistió en que no se trata únicamente de tener talento o condiciones técnicas, sino de comprender qué necesita el equipo en cada momento. «No que sea un virtuoso, que sea un fenómeno, sino que eso es lo que le gusta al aficionado del Real Madrid», añadió. Finalmente, volvió a poner el acento en la entrega del delantero y en su capacidad para no dejar de correr hasta el último instante. «Esa lucha, ese punto de honor, eso al aficionado del Madrid le encanta, sobre todo los últimos minutos, esa heroica, esa lucha, es lo que más le puede gustar a un aficionado del Real Madrid», concluyó.

articles.title: Carlos Espí hace vibrar al Bernabéu
articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: Cuatro goles en 63 minutos, esa es la tarjeta de Espí en lo que va de temporada. Cuatro goles en cuatro ratitos, todos de los que valen victorias necesarias. Él terminó por ser el gran nombre de un partido en el que en la segunda mitad reapareció Vinicius con muy buena pinta, veloz, intenso y certero, pues estuvo en los dos goles, y en el que Bellingham, autor del otro gol madridista, jugó muy bien, con esfuerzo, mando y arrastre. Pero todo queda pequeño ante esta persistencia de Espí para solucionar partidos atascados. Y no son sólo sus goles, sino la impresión plena de que nos hallamos ante un jugadorazo, con cuerpo, ciencia para manejarlo, velocidad, categoría como futbolista y sentido del gol. Un delantero grande para cualquier equipo de alto copete, pero que en el Madrid, con Mbappé en el centro del ataque y el resto de grandes jugadores de la zona delantera, tiene difícil jugar. Lástima, Podría ahorrarle a Mbappé muchos de esos minutos que al final de estas asfixiantes temporadas pesan, pero dudo que el crack francés lo viera bien, porque es un vicioso del fútbol y un ambicioso del gol. Componer un equipo con los dos es difícil, y de hecho sólo ha ocurrido en condiciones desesperadas y ratos breves, cuando se ha sacrificado el orden y la lógica para atacar con todo. Como ayer. Su gol dejó al Celta sin el premio de al menos un punto, que hubiera merecido. En la primera mitad lució un fútbol elegante y bueno, dejando en evidencia al Madrid, despistado y alcanzó el descanso en ventaja bien merecida. El Marid sólo llegó con peligro en un penaltito a Mbappé (si el de Santander fue mitad de cuarto este quizá llegara a cuarto y mitad) que él mismo desperdició. En la segunda mitad espabiló el Madrid, en especial con las entradas en el 55’ de Vinicius, Valverde y Cucurella, pero aun así Courtois tuvo que evitar el 0-2 dando pie a un contraataque vertiginoso del brasileño que acabó en el 1-1 de Bellingham. Luego, arreón creciente hasta el gol salvador de Espí, que se ganó otra medalla.

articles.title: 'I'll take it' - Ryan Naderi's 'lucky punch' keeps Rangers in touch at top
articles.summary: On a Saturday laden with Scottish Premiership goals, Ryan Naderi's was far from the most impressive - but vital for Rangers all the same.
articles.body:
On a Saturday laden with Scottish Premiership goals, Ryan Naderi's was far from the most impressive - but vital for Rangers all the same.

The Czech Republic forward's deflected shot from close range gave his side a 2-1 win at Motherwell and kept the gap between Scottish Premiership leaders Celtic and Rangers at four points.

That could change on Tuesday when resurgent Aberdeen travel to Ibrox for Rangers' game in hand.

But, until then, Rangers supporters will be celebrating the Naderi shot that found the net via a Martin Moormann deflection - a record-equalling 29th goal for a Premiership weekend.

Naderi's scrappy late goal earns Rangers win at Motherwell

We'll only sell if offer makes club blink - McInnes

Three goals in 11 appearances last season was hardly prolific as Naderi adjusted to the hustle and bustle of Scottish football.

Fast forward a few months and the 23-year has 10 in 22 so far this term. Among his goals this season have been winners against Motherwell at Ibrox, Celtic at Celtic Park and Aberdeen in the League Cup semi-final at Hampden.

Such form has led to his first international caps, though goals at that level have so far eluded him in four appearances.

When asked by Sky Sports if he was claiming the winner at Fir Park, rather than it going down as a Moormann own goal, Naderi said: "I'll take it."

"We had a few chances, we didn't score and those moments, you need a stable defence," he said. "We had that lucky punch."

Manager Derek McInnes was similarly delighted.

"When the game is still in the balance and you're putting a bit of pressure on, it's good to know that you've got a bit of evidence there that you can score late winners," he told BBC Scotland.

"I think there's a belief in the team that there's goals, certainly a belief from myself and the staff that we feel there's a goal coming."

And, on Naderi, the manager commented: "I thought it was a proper number nine performance, I've said that to him.

"He ran the channels when he needed to, he pinned defenders when he needed to and he linked the game brilliantly.

"His overall performance was a boy who looks very confident at the minute. I'm so glad we've got him and he should be really proud of what he's producing at the minute."

articles.title: Deion Sanders Says Colorado's Struggles Are 'On Me' amid Growing Hot Seat Speculation
articles.summary: Colorado head coach Deion Sanders took responsibility for the team's disappointing 2026 season following a 35-28 loss to Cincinnati on Saturday.
articles.body:
Colorado head coach Deion Sanders took responsibility for the team's disappointing 2026 season following a 35-28 loss to Cincinnati on Saturday.

"It's on me," Sanders said regarding the Buffaloes' inconsistency, per USA Today's Brent Schrotenboer . "All of it is on me."

Colorado fell to 4-7 with its latest defeat, as the team was eliminated from bowl contention despite beginning the year with a 2-0 record. Speculation surrounding Sanders' job security has continued to increase .

Buffs Drop Bowl Eligibility in Cincy Loss

"I'm not gonna blame nobody," Sanders said, per Schrotenboer. "I've got to do a better job of preparing these guys and getting us ready to play even in situations like it was yesterday evening. But we're not gonna place blame."

While the Buffaloes entered's Saturday's matchup with the worst scoring offense in the Big 12, the majority of their issues came on defense against Cincinnati.

The Bearcats ended the game with 433 total yards, with 225 coming on the ground. Colorado was repeatedly unable to get off the field, as Cincinnati converted 10 of its 15 opportunities on third down.

The Buffaloes still had a chance to score a game-tying touchdown on their final possession of the game, but quarterback Isaac Wilson was picked off to seal the loss.

Colorado has now gone 7-16 in the two years since its impressive 2024 campaign in which the school posted a 9-4 record.

articles.title: Arch Manning Shines, Final Box Score Stats, Highlights, Draft Stock from Texas' Win vs. Arkansas
articles.summary: Arch Manning and the Texas Longhorns cruised to a 45-3 victory over the Arkansas Razorbacks at home Saturday in Austin.
articles.body:
Arch Manning and the Texas Longhorns cruised to a 45-3 victory over the Arkansas Razorbacks at home Saturday in Austin.

Manning and the Longhorns entered their matchup as 18.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook , and walked away with a 42-point win.

The win kept Texas in contention for the SEC championship, as the Longhorns battle the Alabama Crimson Tide for the conference's second spot and a chance to face the Georgia Bulldogs, who can clinch a spot in the title game with a win over the South Carolina Gamecocks on Saturday night.

Texas improved to 9-2 overall and 6-2 in conference play.

(21) South Carolina: 4-4 (CONF), 6-4 (OVR)

The game appeared competitive in the opening quarter, with Texas taking a 14-3 lead. Jelani McDonald returned an interception for a touchdown before Manning added a rushing score.

However, the Longhorns blew the game open before halftime, taking a 31-3 lead with a 17-point second quarter. Manning connected with tight end Emaree Winston for a 21-yard touchdown pass before finding Emmett Mosley V for another score.

Texas continued its offensive surge coming out of halftime, with running back Michael Terry III rushing for a touchdown to extend the lead to 38-3 entering the fourth quarter. With a comfortable 35-point lead and 15 minutes remaining, the Longhorns benched Manning for the final quarter.

Sophomore quarterback KJ Lacey stepped in under center for the remainder of the game, while running back Derrek Cooper joined the scoring action with an 8-yard rushing touchdown to extend the Longhorns' lead to 45-3 and secure the victory.

The senior quarterback dropped three spots on ESPN analyst Mel Kiper Jr.'s most recent Big Board, falling to No. 25 overall and No. 6 among quarterbacks.

The biggest reason being Manning's inconsistency throughout the season, throwing 19 touchdowns and 10 interceptions as the Longhorns sit at 9-2.

The Longhorns dropped back-to-back games in early October, falling 27-24 in both matchups against the unranked Oklahoma State Sooners and Florida Gators. Manning turned the ball over three times between the two losses.

After narrowly escaping the LSU Tigers last week with a 22-21 comeback victory on the road, Manning's inconsistencies remain difficult to overlook for NFL teams. He threw three interceptions in the win, raising questions about which version of Manning the Longhorns will get from game to game.

Manning shined Saturday against the unranked Arkansas Razorbacks, completing 84 percent of his passes without an interception while recording three total touchdowns. However, the performance is unlikely to significantly change opinions on his draft stock.

While the showing demonstrated his ability to take care of business against a four-win program, tougher tests remain as he looks to solidify his NFL prospects.

Texas will close out its regular season on the road against Texas A&M next Friday at 7:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Latest Heisman Trophy 2026 Odds as Jeremiah Smith Rises, Mestemaker Falls
articles.summary: Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith remains the clear favorite to win this year's Heisman Trophy after catching six passes for 165 yards and two touchdowns in a 31-28 road loss to Nebraska on Saturday afternoon.
articles.body:
Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith remains the clear favorite to win this year's Heisman Trophy after catching six passes for 165 yards and two touchdowns in a 31-28 road loss to Nebraska on Saturday afternoon.

According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the current odds have Smith as a -360 favorite, giving him implied odds of 78.26 percent to win.

After the 3:30 p.m. ET window of games on Saturday, here's a look at the players listed on FanDuel's board.

Oklahoma State QB Drew Mestemaker: +12500

Smith got Ohio State on the board early after outracing Nebraska's coverage and hauling in a 67-yard touchdown.

Nebraska then scored 21 unanswered points to take a two-touchdown lead. However, Smith continued his dominance and snagged a 31-yard score in the back of the end zone to help cut the Cornhuskers' lead in half before halftime.

Smith has now caught 86 passes for 1,482 yards and 17 touchdowns. He's caught at least four passes for 68 yards in all 11 of his games. He's scored a touchdown in all but one of his contests. Smith is still producing despite QB1 Julian Sayin suffering an undisclosed injury to his throwing arm on Oct. 17 against Indiana that has kept him out of action ever since.

Smith is the best player in college football, and there really isn't any denying that fact at this point.

Although Ohio State has endured a difficult 7-4 season that will leave the Buckeyes out of the College Football Playoff, Smith certainly deserves the Heisman. He has one more regular season game against Michigan next Saturday at noon ET.

At this juncture, it's hard seeing anyone else win the Heisman, even though quarterbacks have won 20 of the last 25 Heismans. Miami QB Darian Mensah has the best case considering his team's standing (No. 7 in the College Football Playoff) and his own stats (29 touchdowns, 3,076 yards). Mensah will assuredly be a finalist, but he's an underdog to win (at the moment, anyway).

Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker had a case earlier this season, but the Cowboys' recent performance doesn't help the cause. The unranked Cowboys have lost three of their last five games to fall to 6-4 overall. Oklahoma State has allowed 29.7 points (112th in Division I FBS), so that's not on Mestemaker, who also entered Saturday leading Division I FBS with 3,239 yards and 30 touchdowns.

However, Mestemaker had a tough day last Saturday in a 52-27 loss vs. No. 12 Texas Tech, throwing for 277 yards (his lowest mark since a Week 1 loss to Tulsa, 24-10) and two interceptions (one touchdown).

Still, Mestemaker has impressed since arriving from North Texas via the transfer portal and could very well be making his home in the NFL soon enough (the B/R NFL Scouting Department placed Mestemaker third to the Miami Dolphins in its latest mock draft).

articles.title: Rutgers Stuns PSU with Must-See Lateral TD at Goal Line, Walk-Off 2-Point Conversion for Upset Win
articles.summary: Rutgers football broke an 18-game losing streak against Penn State in the most dramatic way possible, scoring a touchdown off a lateral with no time remaining before converting a two-point conversion to cap a 15-point fourth-quarter run en route to a 25-24 road win.
articles.body:
Rutgers football broke an 18-game losing streak against Penn State in the most dramatic way possible, scoring a touchdown off a lateral with no time remaining before converting a two-point conversion to cap a 15-point fourth-quarter run en route to a 25-24 road win.

The Scarlet Knights, 25.5-point underdogs per FanDuel Sportsbook , initially appeared to lose the game after AJ Surace's fourth-down pass in the end zone to wide receiver Ben Black III fell incomplete. However, a defensive pass interference call gave the Scarlet Knights another chance.

Rutgers took advantage on its second shot. Surace threw the ball to Raymond out wide, but the running back got stuffed. However, he made a brilliant play and threw a chest pass to Black, who ran in for the score.

The Scarlet Knights decided to end the game right there and went for two. Surace dropped back to pass, looked right in the flat and saw a wide-open David Gilley, who rolled in untouched for the score.

This has largely been a difficult season for 3-8 (2-6 Big Ten) Rutgers, which had lost four straight by a total of 87 points entering Saturday. Saturday's win represented the Scarlet Knights' first against Penn State since 1988.

As for the Nittany Lions, this is inarguably one of the most difficult losses in program history amid a tough first season in the Matt Campbell era. PSU had enjoyed some momentum of late after losing its first four Big Ten games by winning three straight, but a brutal home loss washed that away.

Both teams end their regular seasons on Saturday. Rutgers will host Michigan State, and Penn State will visit Maryland.

articles.title: No. 4 UCLA Upset by Michigan, How Loss Impacts CFP Bracket Outlook After Ty Dieffenbach Injury
articles.summary: No. 4 UCLA's hopes of an undefeated season are over.
articles.body:
No. 4 UCLA's hopes of an undefeated season are over.

The Bruins conceded their first defeat of the season Saturday night with an 18-16 triple-overtime loss at unranked Michigan in which quarterback Ty Dieffenbach suffered a serious injury.

Dieffenbach took a hit on the opening play of the first overtime and was down on the field for minutes before he was carted off the field.

UCLA came in at No. 4 on the latest College Football Playoff rankings following their 10-0 start to the season.

Here's a look at how the other top teams in the last CFP rankings are doing as of Saturday evening.

No. 3 Alabama (9-2) won 47-0 against visiting Chattanooga

No. 5 Texas (9-2) won 45-3 versus Arkansas

No. 8 Indiana (9-2) lost 27-24 at Washington in OT

No. 9 Tennessee (8-2) won 27-13 versus LSU

No. 12 Texas Tech (10-1) won 20-10 at Baylor

No. 10 BYU (9-2) won 31-29 at Kansas in OT

No. 11 Wake Forest (10-1) won 50-29 at Georgia Tech

No. 13 Oregon (8-3) won 45-7 at Michigan State

No. 14 Ohio State (7-4) lost 31-28 at Nebraska

No. 1 Georgia (9-1) at No. 21 South Carolina, 7:30 p.m. ET

No. 6 Notre Dame (9-1) versus SMU, 7:30 p.m. ET

No. 7 Miami (9-1) versus Virginia Tech, 7:30 p.m. ET

The Bruins weren't the only Big Ten team whose CFP ranking likely took a hit Saturday.

Ohio State was the first top-14 team in the CFP rankings to lose Saturday after conceding a defeat to unranked Nebraska that likely put the four-loss Buckeyes out of playoff contention.

Indiana later suffered their second conference loss of the season with an overtime defeat at Washington.

UCLA could secure a place in the CFP rankings ahead of the defending national champions by closing out the regular season with a win next Saturday against visiting No. 18 USC.

The Bruins' chances in that crucial game could hinge on the status of Dieffenbach, who took over as his team's starting quarterback after Nico Iamaleava suffered a season-ending knee injury in October.

Madden Iamaleava entered Saturday's game in relief of Dieffenbach and went 0-for-1 while looking understandably overwhelmed.

If Dieffenbach is forced to miss time, whether Iamaleava is able to step up in what would be his first start of the season will shape where UCLA ultimately ends up when the final CFP rankings are published Dec. 12.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin, LSU Drop 3rd Straight Game with Loss to Tennessee, Final Box Score Stats & Highlights
articles.summary: The Tennessee Volunteers defeated Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers, 27-13, in Knoxville, Tennessee, on Saturday.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Volunteers defeated Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers, 27-13, in Knoxville, Tennessee, on Saturday.

LSU entered the road matchup as 1.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook , but struggled to build momentum behind costly turnovers, finishing with three total.

Tennessee had its fair share of mistakes, turning the ball over three times, while three different players took snaps at quarterback. Faizon Brandon got the start before George MacIntyre took over as the primary passer. The two alternated at quarterback for the remainder of the game.

The win improved Tennessee to 6-2 in conference play and 9-2 overall, keeping the Volunteers in contention for the SEC Championship as they battle the Alabama Crimson Tide and Texas Longhorns for a potential second-place finish.

Tennessee holds the head-to-head tiebreaker over Alabama after defeating the Crimson Tide 26-10 in October but does not have the same advantage over Texas, falling to the Longhorns 20-17 earlier this season.

(21) South Carolina: 4-4 (CONF), 6-4 (OVR)

Both teams looked sloppy out of the gate, with LSU turning the ball over once on a fumble and Tennessee twice on an interception and a fumble.

After struggling in the opening quarter, Brandon was pulled and replaced by MacIntyre, who did not start after suffering a knee injury against Texas A&M a week earlier, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel.

LSU took a 6-0 lead after the first quarter behind a pair of field goals from Scott Starzyk.

The Volunteers got on the scoreboard at the 8:10 mark of the second quarter with a 52-yard field goal before their defense forced a fumble to secure another turnover.

Tennessee took its first lead as the clock wound down in the second quarter, with MacIntyre connecting with DaSaahn Brame for the game's first touchdown to take a 10-6 lead into halftime.

A field goal extended Tennessee's lead to 13-6, but a fumble on a punt gave LSU a short field. The Tigers capitalized on the next possession as Leavitt found Trey'Dez Green for a touchdown to tie the game at 13 after three quarters.

The Vols proceeded to dominate the fourth quarter, outscoring Kiffin's Tigers 14-0 to salt away another big win in their pursuit of a College Football Playoff berth.

Tennessee will close out its regular season against Vanderbilt on the road next Saturday, while LSU will hit the road to face the Arkansas Razorbacks.

articles.title: No. 8 Indiana Upset by Washington in OT, How Loss Impacts Hoosiers' CFP Bracket Outlook
articles.summary: The No. 8 Indiana Hoosiers suffered a crushing 27-24 loss in double overtime against the Washington Huskies on Saturday.
articles.body:
The No. 8 Indiana Hoosiers suffered a crushing 27-24 loss in double overtime against the Washington Huskies on Saturday.

Indiana entered the game with an 88.7 percent chance to make the College Football Playoff, per ESPN . The loss could drop Indiana's chances down to 49.9 percent, according to projections from The Rooting Guide .

Indiana had an opportunity to tie the game, but kicker Paddy McAteer missed a 37-yard field goal attempt to end things in Seattle. Coach Curt Cignetti benched kicker Nico Radicic after a blocked field goal earlier in the game.

Indiana fell five spots in the rankings during their bye as skeptics questioned the strength of their schedule. Although the Hoosiers climbed up one spot after their 27-13 win over the USC Trojans, Saturday's loss will surely see them tumble down the rankings once again.

Indiana dropped into a tie for second place in the Big Ten alongside the Oregon Ducks and Iowa Hawkeyes. To make it to the conference championship game, Indiana would need to defeat Purdue while Nebraska defeats Iowa and the Huskies defeat Oregon, according to USA Today 's Paul Myerberg .

Cignetti has ripped the selection committee for showing favoritism towards the SEC, but the loss certainly won't help his case. Indiana has just one win against a top-25 ranked team, and although the Hoosiers entered Saturday's game with a 9-1 record, they ranked behind multiple two-loss SEC teams in the most recent rankings.

Other teams on the playoff bubble — No. 10 BYU, No. 11 Wake Forest, No. 12 Texas Tech and No. 13 Oregon — won their Week 12 games.

The Hoosiers are now 9-2 overall and 6-2 in the Big Ten. They will host Purdue for their regular-season finale in the Old Oaken Bucket game next week.

articles.title: QB Ty Dieffenbach carted off the field in OT as No. 4 UCLA's undefeated season ends with loss to Michigan
articles.summary: Dieffenbach was injured on the first play of overtime.
articles.body:
UCLA's undefeated season is over, and the Bruins might be down to their third quarterback.

Ty Dieffenbach was injured on the first play of overtime in the No. 4 Bruins' 18-16 triple-overtime loss at Michigan . Dieffenbach ran to the right and appeared to suffer a serious injury when he was tackled.

After he was helped up off the turf, Dieffenbach was immediately strapped to a stretcher while sitting up slightly and carted off the field. He was replaced by Madden Iamaleava, the younger brother of Week 1 starter Nico Iamaleava. The elder Iamaleava suffered a season-ending left knee injury in UCLA's win over Oregon, and Dieffenbach has been the team's No. 1 QB since.

After Dieffenbach was injured, UCLA failed to get a first down and had to kick a field goal. Michigan responded with a field goal, and the two teams traded kicks in the second overtime.

In the third overtime, Iamaleava was indecisive as UCLA's mandated two-point attempt amounted to nothing. Then Michigan QB Bryce Underwood found Jalen Hoffman in the end zone for the Wolverines' winning points.

In the second overtime, Iamaleava also had the chance to run for a first down and then some as he escaped the pocket on third down. Instead, he stayed behind the line of scrimmage before throwing an incomplete pass to set up UCLA's game-tying field goal.

Underwood started his first game since he was benched at halftime of the Wolverines' comeback win against Penn State on Oct. 17. His go-ahead TD pass in the fourth quarter was also the first TD he'd thrown since he threw two in a 20-19 loss to Iowa. That game happened on Sept. 26.

Saturday showed that Michigan has a defense capable of powering it to a playoff with a simply average offense. Michigan's offense has been anything but average.

The Wolverines' only TD of the game was the product of a 15-yard drive, thanks to a Dieffenbach fumble. Dieffenbach fumbled one other time and also had an interception.

Michigan mustered just 247 yards of total offense on 67 plays as Underwood was 11-of-24 passing for 127 yards and a TD, and Savion Hiter rushed 26 times for 104 yards.

Could the Bruins really go from being a playoff lock to being on the precipice of missing out on the 12-team field entirely?

UCLA has No. 18 USC in Week 13 and Madden Iamaleava will get the start assuming Dieffenbach will be unable to go. A loss to the Trojans coupled with a longer-term injury for Dieffenbach would leave UCLA at 10-2 with a third-string quarterback. Would the committee deem the Bruins worthy of a playoff spot if they fail to make the Big Ten title game?

Just three years ago, Florida State missed out on the four-team playoff because of a season-ending injury to QB Jordan Travis and subsequent offensive struggles over the Seminoles' final two games. Could the same cruel thing happen to UCLA?

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Winners and Losers from Week 12
articles.summary: The normal warning applied. When you think the schedule is soft, college football tends to have a different idea.
articles.body:
The normal warning applied. When you think the schedule is soft, college football tends to have a different idea.

The only ranked matchup on the slate is No. 1 Georgia's trip to No. 21 South Carolina. Otherwise, the rest of the Top 25 met an unranked opponent—and we've already had a few massive results.

While several teams escaped a tough game, three Big Ten programs fell on the road. UCLA, in particular, saw its unbeaten record fade away.

And the chaos may just be getting started.

This piece will be updated Saturday night.

Two weeks ago, a lopsided loss to Oregon appeared to doom Ohio State. The setback sent the Buckeyes to 6-3, tumbling to 20th in the CFP rankings.

But then, a bit of hope. The madness of last Saturday's drama-filled slate allowed Ryan Day's team to climb six spots to 14th, putting the Buckeyes in position to hope for chaos in front of them and sneak into the Playoff.

Ohio State stumbled in a trip to Nebraska, which snapped a 31-game losing skid against AP-ranked opponents.

There, officially, will be no Big Ten title for Ohio State, no trip to the College Football Playoff. Instead, the Buckeyes are left hoping for a rivalry win over Michigan and star receiver Jeremiah Smith to hoist the Heisman Trophy.

Every year, the College Football Playoff selection committee loves to tell us how much they're watching the games.

Since losing to Miami in mid-September, Wake Forest has notched eight straight wins. Saturday's 50-29 rout of Georgia Tech—it was 43-7 in the third quarter, mind you—marked the seventh consecutive triumph of 21-plus points.

Wake isn't simply beating teams. No, the Gio Lopez-led Demon Deacons are shredding everyone in their path. He accounted for 342 yards and four touchdowns at Tech before sitting out the whole fourth quarter.

If the committee is actually paying attention, the next CFP Top 25 should feature a red-hot 10-1 Wake Forest soaring in the Top 10.

Within the 12-team CFP field, one invitation will be extended to the highest-ranked program in the Group of 6 leagues.

And that group of contenders is shrinking.

Friday night, Mountain West favorite New Mexico dropped Wyoming to 7-3 and out of contention. Memphis and North Texas followed suit on Saturday, falling to Navy and Tulane, respectively, for a third and fourth overall loss. Even if they win a conference title, the trio is effectively out.

Along with UNM, Air Force and Toledo won on Friday. Liberty took care of business on Saturday, while current G6 front-runner Boise State and Louisiana Tech—as of writing—haven't yet played in Week 12. The race is still far from decided.

But there are only a handful of true threats left.

It's not entirely proper to say Texas has clinched a spot in the College Football Playoff. We don't completely know that.

Based on how much the committee reveres both the SEC and the Longhorns' résumé, however, they're awfully close. Saturday's painless 45-3 win at Arkansas lifted Steve Sarkisian's team to 9-2 on the season.

Yes, the Horns travel to Texas A&M next week. Especially in a lost season for A&M, the Aggies will be motivated to play the spoiler role.

But even at 9-3, Texas would have a bunch of marquee wins—including a head-to-head result over Tennessee that could sway the committee despite a third loss. (Yes, I hear you about Alabama, Vols fans. I don't control this.)

Texas, with a victory over A&M, is definitely in.

And it's plausible the Horns already are, too.

Sometimes, it's not pretty. Maybe the offense struggled, the defense was rough. There were penalties, turnovers or blown leads. Any number of adverse issues.

No matter the context, that's the job: Find a way.

Tenth-ranked BYU squandered a 10-point fourth-quarter lead at Kansas and yielded a crushing touchdown on 4th-and-goal in the second overtime period. Nevertheless, the Cougs escaped with a 31-29 win in triple OT.

During the afternoon window, No. 9 Tennessee had a scrap with former coach Lane Kiffin and his reeling LSU team. It took 55 solid minutes, but the Vols ultimately put away the visitors 27-13. Similar story for No. 12 Texas Tech, which needed a late field goal to ice a 20-10 triumph at Baylor.

BYU's ceiling is sketchy, Tennessee's offense is a concern and Texas Tech has played quite a few competitive fourth quarters lately.

If you're a fan of UCLA or Indiana, I'm sorry. Losses hurt, and upsets add an extra layer of disappointment to the situation.

Team Chaos, on the other hand, is thriving in the Big Ten.

No. 4 UCLA took its undefeated record out to Michigan, which used a stellar defensive performance to spring an 18-16 upset in triple OT. Adding injury to insult, UCLA lost quarterback Ty Dieffenbach—who replaced Nico Iamaleava (torn left ACL) earlier this season—to an unspecified, seemingly serious health issue.

Just about simultaneously, No. 8 Indiana missed a potential game-tying field goal in overtime and lost 27-24 at Washington.

Suddenly, Week 13 will be loaded with intrigue in the Big Ten.

UCLA remains in control as the conference's lone one-loss team, but the Bruins may be underdogs against rival USC if Dieffenbach is sidelined. Oregon has renewed life in the league standings thanks to IU's loss, and Iowa has a path to the Big Ten Championship Game, too.

Buckle up, my friends, and keep that scenario list handy next Saturday.

articles.title: Rutgers beats Penn State for first time since 1988 with last-second lateral near goal line, 2-point conversion
articles.summary: The Scarlet Knights snapped an 18-game losing streak against the Nittany Lions with a stunner at Beaver Stadium.
articles.body:
A last-second lateral set the stage for one of the most memorable wins in recent Rutgers history on Saturday night at Penn State's Beaver Stadium.

Scarlet Knights running back Antwan Raymond caught a pass from quarterback AJ Surace in the flat on first-and-goal with his team trailing 24-17 and mere seconds remaining. He put on a move but was still wrangled well short of the goal line. As he was going down to the ground, with the clock about to hit triple zeroes, Raymond threw a point-blank chest-pass backward to wide receiver Ben Black III.

Black corralled it, took a few steps and found pay dirt.

Instead of playing for overtime, Rutgers head coach Greg Schiano decided to go for the win. Surace hit running back Clay Thevenin out of the backfield for the game-winning 2-point conversion. Those unforgettable moments capped an 11-play, 67-yard drive that was furthered by a pair of Penn State pass interference penalties, the second of which arrived on fourth-and-8 deep in Nittany Lions territory.

Rutgers ended up walking it off in State College with a gripping 25-24 victory , beating Penn State for the first time since 1988.

The Scarlet Knights (3-8, 2-6 Big Ten) had lost 18 consecutive games to the Nittany Lions (6-5, 3-5).

Although Raymond didn't get in the end zone before his heady lateral, he finished with 101 yards and two touchdowns on the ground.

Rutgers found itself in a 16-0 hole in the second quarter and faced a 24-10 deficit heading into the fourth quarter.

The Scarlet Knights scored a combined 10 points in their previous two outings, blowout defeats to Wisconsin and Nebraska. They logged a pair of touchdowns in the final frame of Saturday's game at Penn State.

The first one stemmed from a 19-play drive that began in the third quarter and concluded in the fourth after more than 9 ½ minutes of possession.

Not much has gone right for Rutgers this season. Saturday marks the team's first win since Oct. 17 and just its second victory over an FBS squad during the 2026 campaign. Earlier this month, Rutgers athletic director Keli Zinn announced that Schiano will return for 2027 season , which will be his 19th total leading the Scarlet Knights, including his eighth consecutive in his second stint at the helm.

Schiano hasn't been able to deliver Rutgers the kind of success it achieved under him in the Big East. His Scarlet Knights have yet to wrap Big Ten play with a winning record versus conference opponents. They won't come close to that mark this time around, either.

At least on Saturday, his Rutgers team conjured up some much-needed magic on the road against a longtime regional power, adding to the chaos of a league that also saw No. 4 UCLA fall to Michigan in triple overtime and No. 8 Indiana lose to Washington in OT around the same exact time.

articles.title: LSU's Lane Kiffin Era Is College Football's Biggest Disappointment
articles.summary: Almost a year ago to the day, the drama receded. With the college football world anxiously awaiting his final decision, Lane Kiffin bolted a CFB Playoff team playing for the allure and overflowing potential of LSU.
articles.body:
Almost a year ago to the day, the drama receded. With the college football world anxiously awaiting his final decision, Lane Kiffin bolted a CFB Playoff team playing for the allure and overflowing potential of LSU.

On Saturday, the Tigers lost their third consecutive game and fifth loss of the season.

Brian Kelly never lost five games at LSU, and it still wasn't good enough to save his job. And when Ed Orgeron lost his sixth game for the Tigers in 2021, just two years removed from a perfect season and a national championship, he was asked to leave, albeit with a hefty payday.

Biggest 5-Star Recruiting Busts of Past Decade 👎

On Saturday night, Kiffin came up woefully short against his former team, capping off an unremarkable season in unremarkable fashion. In fact, LSU's 27-13 loss to Tennessee was a perfect encapsulation of what we've seen all year.

Tantalizing potential and shockingly sloppy play. Not enough offense. Not enough defense.

Like every game this season, the Tigers were competitive. And like many games this season, they collapsed in the most important moments.

The Tigers turned the ball over three times, including a critical fumble from quarterback Sam Leavitt. Over the last three games, LSU turned the ball over eight times. Perhaps even more jarring, the Tigers committed 16 penalties on Saturday night, the most it has committed in a single game in more than 30 years.

Given the buzz surrounding Kiffin's arrival and the investment LSU made into its roster and staff, spending north of $40 million on its roster , it's hard not to look at Kiffin's debut season as nothing but shocking, smoldering disappointment.

And along the way, there's been drama. It's a Lane Kiffin-coached team, so perhaps this part is assumed.

Last week, Leavitt was criticized for leaving the Tiger Stadium field after losing to Texas before singing the alma mater. He shrugged off those criticisms by saying he wasn't on social media .

This week? The camera found him screaming at his offensive line after a bad snap put the team in a bind. Needless to say, Kiffin will likely be looking for a new quarterback soon.

On the topic of his roster, Kiffin couldn't help himself this week. When reflecting on his team, he seemed to hit the fast forward button on this season and look to the future.

"We'll have better rosters, and that's no poor reflection upon these players," he told reporters . "We just will. We will have been there. We will have built depth. We will. We won't have Senior Days with 2 scholarship players."

Perhaps no comment that Kiffin has made over the last few years, and there are plenty to pick apart, misses the mark more than this.

Forget about the tens of millions of dollars that he had at his disposal to attract enormously talented players or the advantages that come from coaching at arguably the best college football job in the country.

Kiffin, in essence, is talking about building for the future. But this is not a place that allows for such serenity to exist, nor does it much care for excuses.

In fact, Kiffin knows better. He has to know better.

He took this job knowing fully what the expectations were. And when he did, he never imagined in his wildest dreams he would be standing before a group of reporters talking about the agony of his fifth loss.

The fact that he would discredit his own roster creation in an effort to spin a message of long-term building is frankly insulting.

Kiffin will continue to build his roster with ample resources, and the talent will continue to come to Baton Rouge, just like always. But the fact that he had to say this part out loud rather than accept this team, the one he handpicked, is a concerning glimpse into his psyche of a man who might be in over his head.

The turnovers, the penalties and the close calls against elite teams have shown us that talent hasn't been the issue for Kiffin's group, no matter what he wants to say. In fact, at many points this group looked like one of the deepest in all of America.

This is not a talent issue; it's something else. And it starts squarely with him.

No team this season did less with more. What a waste.

Over the past year, we've been building toward this moment. Only rather than barely being bowl eligible, we assumed LSU would be in the mix to compete for an SEC title or a College Football Playoff berth once we hit late November.

Instead, it's another lost season for a program where lost seasons can't exist. Only now they do, they're just far more expensive than they used to be.

Nine qualifying places required three things to happen: Palmeiras winning the Libertadores, Atlético-MG winning the Copa Sudamericana and Grêmio being relegated. The Copa Sudamericana winners would qualify directly for the 2027 Libertadores group stage; with Atlético-MG also set to finish high in the Brasileirão, their league qualification place would have been reallocated, opening up a spot for the ninth-placed club.

articles.title: Tennessee defense ruins Lane Kiffin's return to Neyland Stadium | Adams
articles.summary: Tennessee's offense succeeded in spurts. Its defense was relentless all game long.
articles.body:
An imperfect game produced the perfect ending act for Tennessee football in a 27-13 victory over LSU on Nov. 21 at Neyland Stadium.

A defense that has carried the Vols all season lifted them up one more time with LSU driving toward a possible tying touchdown in the fourth quarter.

Blitzing linebacker Edwin Spillman knocked the ball loose from LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt, and safety Dejuan Lane recovered for the Vols. That was the beginning of the end for the Tigers.

There's nothing surprising about UT's defense delivering a game-turning play. But no one who watched the first quarter could have guessed that quarterback Faizon Brandon would have the final say.

Brandon, a surprise starter, had two turnovers to set up two early LSU field goals. But he made up for those turnovers by running for two fourth-quarter touchdowns as the Vols (9-2, 6-2 SEC) moved ever closer to their second College Football Playoff berth in three seasons.

His 55-yard touchdown run with just over four minutes to play put the game out of LSU's reach. Minutes later, Tennessee fans celebrated by throwing debris.

The Vols were on their way to a rousing victory over Lane Kiffin, the coach their fans love to hate. Unlike Kiffin's previous visits to Neyland – as an Ole Miss coach and an Alabama assistant coach – this trip ended in defeat for the former Tennessee coach.

He's now 0-2 this season against the fans who hate him the most. LSU lost in September at Oxford to Ole Miss, whom Kiffin abandoned in favor of the Tigers last season.

Kiffin coached Tennessee for one season in 2009 before making a fast break to a head-coaching job at Southern California.

Fans don't forget such departures. And you can be sure Ole Miss fans were cheering just as hard as Tennessee's when the Vols put the finishing touches on the victory.

Those fans only cared about the outcome, not how inartistically it was achieved.

Tennessee and LSU each had three turnovers. The two teams also combined for 28 penalties, including 16 by LSU.

LSU had every opportunity to take command of the game early. And it failed spectacularly for the same reasons it usually does in close games.

The Tigers were penalized 11 times in the half. Most notably, star safety Ty Benefield was ejected for targeting to set up a Tennessee touchdown that gave it a 10-6 halftime lead.

Tennessee was anything but mistake-free itself. Brandon lost a fumble and threw an interception to set up two Scott Starzyk field goals.

Once Heupel replaced Brandon with George MacIntyre, the offense perked up. Yards didn't come easily, but the Vols gained just enough of them to drive 34 yards for a touchdown on their last possession of the half.

Tennessee's offense came in spurts. Its defense was relentless from start to finish. Whenever LSU was on the verge of offensive momentum, UT's defense got in the way.

That defense has been stifling all year under new coordinator Jim Knowles. It's not showing signs of fatigue, though. In fact, it's getting better.

The Vols held Kentucky to six points and Texas A&M to seven in their two previous games. LSU, which leads the SEC in total offense, also had little success against Tennessee.

UT's defense had one huge slip-up against the Tigers, who gained possession on the Tennessee 9-yard-line after Qua Moss mishandled a high-bouncing punt and LSU recovered.

Leavitt faked deftly to his running back before 6-foot-7 tight end Trey'Dez Green slipped unguarded into the Tennessee end zone. Leavitt had an easy toss for the touchdown.

John Adams is a senior columnist. He may be reached at 865-342-6284 or john.adams@knoxnews.com.

articles.title: Kyle Whittingham Addresses Michigan Job Security Following Stunning UCLA Upset
articles.summary: Kyle Whittingham addresses his uncertain Michigan future following a stunning win over No. 4 UCLA and reveals an emotional tribute to Warde Manuel.
articles.body:
Kyle Whittingham just delivered the biggest victory of his brief tenure as Michigan's head coach, but whether he'll be around to build on it remains a major question. Following the Wolverines' stunning 18-16 triple-overtime victory over No. 4 UCLA on Saturday, Whittingham was asked about his job security and what the university's upcoming leadership change could mean for his future.

Rather than making any bold declarations, the veteran coach acknowledged the uncertainty surrounding his position while expressing appreciation for outgoing athletic director Warde Manuel. He also made it clear that Saturday's victory was an important moment for a Michigan program that has endured a frustrating season.

Kyle Whittingham Addresses Uncertain Michigan Future

When asked about his job security following the victory, Whittingham admitted that the decisions concerning Michigan's future leadership are largely out of his control. He then offered an emotional tribute to Manuel, who gave him the opportunity to lead the Wolverines.

"Yeah, well, the change is above my pay grade," Whittingham said. "Just waiting to see what the change actually turns out to be."

Whittingham continued by thanking Manuel for his support throughout his first season in Ann Arbor. The Michigan coach also revealed that the team honored the outgoing athletic director following Saturday's emotional victory.

"I can say it's been a pleasure working for Warde Manuel during these first 10 months here in Michigan. He gave me the opportunity to coach this team, and we'll miss him and actually gave him the game ball tonight. We had to give the game ball in the locker room tonight."

Whittingham added that he appreciated the relationship they developed despite its relatively short duration. He described their time together as a successful partnership, even though it is nearing its conclusion.

"So that's been a very good partnership in my estimation, even though it didn't last very long."

Michigan's Victory Over UCLA Could Change the Conversation

The Wolverines entered Saturday's matchup with a 5-5 record, needing one more victory to become bowl eligible. Against an undefeated UCLA team ranked No. 4 in the College Football Playoff standings, Michigan appeared to face an uphill battle.

Instead, the Wolverines pulled off an improbable 18-16 victory in triple overtime , improving to 6-5 and securing bowl eligibility. The victory also handed UCLA its first loss of the season and potentially complicated the Bruins' College Football Playoff hopes.

For Whittingham, the win represented something much bigger than simply adding another victory to Michigan's record. It gave his team a much-needed positive moment during a season that has generated considerable criticism.

"But going forward, this win, I don't know exactly how to compare it to working with new guys," Whittingham said. "But it was big for our program, I'll tell you that."

Those comments come as questions surrounding Whittingham's future continue to dominate discussions about Michigan football. CBS Sports previously reported that industry sources believe the Wolverines could consider another coaching change after just one season.

Will Michigan Keep Kyle Whittingham for 2027?

The uncertainty surrounding Whittingham has only intensified with Michigan preparing for a significant change in athletic department leadership. Former Texas A&M athletic director Trev Alberts is expected to replace Manuel, potentially giving the Wolverines a new decision-maker shortly after the regular season concludes.

According to reporting about Michigan's athletic director transition , Alberts is expected to begin his new position on December 1. That would come just three days after Michigan's regular-season finale against Ohio State.

Michigan has already examined several potential coaching replacements , with CBS Sports identifying five prominent candidates who could enter the conversation if Whittingham departs. However, no decision has been announced regarding the veteran coach's future.

The victory over UCLA certainly strengthens Whittingham's argument that he deserves another season, particularly considering the Wolverines were significant underdogs against one of the nation's top teams. Still, bowl eligibility alone may not be enough to settle a decision involving Michigan's next athletic director.

Whittingham now has one more opportunity to make his case before the regular season ends. And it happens to come against Michigan's biggest rival.

Michigan will travel to Columbus next Saturday to face Ohio State in a matchup that could have enormous implications for Whittingham's future. The Wolverines will enter the contest with renewed confidence following their upset of UCLA, while the Buckeyes are coming off a surprising loss to Nebraska.

A victory over Ohio State would give Michigan two consecutive wins against highly ranked opponents to close the regular season. It would also provide Whittingham with a significantly stronger argument for remaining in Ann Arbor.

For now, the 66-year-old coach isn't making promises about his future or pretending he controls the decisions being made above him. Instead, he's focused on the significance of Saturday's victory and appreciative of the man who brought him to Michigan.

Whittingham gave Warde Manuel the game ball after beating UCLA. Whether Michigan's new leadership gives Whittingham another season remains to be seen.

articles.title: Messi, Miami stunned by Columbus in MLS playoff opener
articles.summary: Lionel Messi's bid to win back-to-back MLS Cup titles suffered a blow on Saturday as 10-man Inter Miami were thumped 3-0 at home by Columbus Crew in their fi...
articles.body:
Lionel Messi's bid to win back-to-back MLS Cup titles suffered a blow on Saturday as 10-man Inter Miami were thumped 3-0 at home by Columbus Crew in their first-round playoff series opener.

Two goals from Chile international Gonzalo Tapia either side of a Taha Habroune second-half strike secured a deserved victory for Crew in front of a shellshocked crowd at Miami's Nu Stadium.

The result means seventh seeds Columbus, the 2023 champions, can eliminate Messi and Miami from the playoffs with a victory in game two of the best-of-three series in Ohio next Friday.

On Saturday's evidence, Columbus will head into game two confident of finishing the job after tearing Miami to shreds.

The 24-year-old Tapia was a menace throughout, winning an early penalty after being brought down by Miami goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair before stepping up to convert the spot-kick.

Miami's task got harder in the 36th minute when Gonzalo Lujan was sent off after receiving a second yellow card for a reckless late challenge on the Crew's Stephen Moreira.

Columbus's US international goalkeeper Patrick Schulte, meanwhile, thwarted Miami's attempts to get back in the game, including one diving save to deny Messi a trademark free-kick.

Messi was fortunate to escape dismissal on half-time, when he appeared to direct a throw-in into Tapia's face at point-blank range as frustrations boiled over.

Columbus made the game safe early in the second half with two goals in six minutes.

A fine flowing counter-attack ended with Harbroune coolly slotting past St.Clair in the 52nd minute before Tapia made it 3-0 in the 58th minute, punishing slack marking by Miami's Yannick Bright to go clean through on goal.

"It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them," Miami coach Kily Gonzalez said afterwards.

"We didn't produce the great performance we had hoped for. Everything went wrong, but we have to learn from it because next time, if we don't win, we're out," he added. "There's no better challenge for us as a team than this. It's a test of character, and I know my team has that character."

In other MLS playoff action on Saturday, Joaquin Valiente scored two goals as host Dallas beat Portland 3-0 in their Western Conference series opener.

The 25-year-old Uruguayan midfielder scored in the 53rd and 55th minutes and Samuel Sarver added an insurance goal in the fourth minute of stoppage time for Dallas, who can advance by winning at Portland next Saturday.

US teen Peyton Miller scored one goal and set up another in New England's 2-0 victory over visiting Philadelphia.

Miller's 10th-minute shot deflected in off Philadelphia defender Nathan Harriel to make it 1-0 and the 19-year-old scored in the 73rd minute off a Jack Harrison cross to complete the scoring.

New England can advance to the MLS Eastern Conference semi-finals with a road victory next Saturday.
